title: bug: headless worker launches --continue on stale session ID after DB seed failure causing worker_noop_zero_output
body:
## Summary

PRRT workers suffer `worker_noop_zero_output` when stored OpenCode session ID cannot be seeded into the worker isolated DB but launch proceeds with `--session <stale-id> --continue`.

## Root cause

`headless-runtime-model.sh:497-499` always appends `--session $persisted_session --continue` from provider_sessions DB.

`headless-runtime-invoke.sh:132-137` logs `db_seed_failed` but continues launching opencode anyway.

Result: opencode gets `--session <stale-id> --continue` in a fresh isolated DB where that session does not exist → exits code 0, zero output.

## Why retry guard misses it

`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:363-369` retries only when exit nonzero OR output contains "Session not found". OpenCode exits 0 silently → bypassed.

## Impact

690/733 stored PRRT session rows missing from shared OpenCode DB. Workers dispatch, produce zero output, exit 0. PRRT loops with infrastructure-failure backoff.

## Fix

When `db_seed_failed`: remove `--session`/`--continue` from command and start fresh session. Or add retry guard for clean-exit + zero-output → treat as session_not_found.

## Affected files

- `headless-runtime-model.sh:497-499` — adds --session/--continue
- `headless-runtime-invoke.sh:132-137` — seed failure not authoritative
- `headless-runtime-attempt.sh:363-369` — retry guard misses clean-exit zero-output
- `headless-runtime-failure.sh:683-694` — classifies as worker_noop_zero_output

title: Pulse check should report retained supervisor permission blockers and safe worker-count diagnostics
body:
## What

Make pulse diagnostics distinguish a healthy idle runner from retained or stale pulse permission blockers, and document an interactive-safe active-worker count path that does not require sourcing pulse-wrapper.sh. Deliverables: 1) pulse-check-helper.sh report surfaces retained/unverified supervisor-pulse permission blockers from worker-progress-blockers.jsonl even when runtime failure thresholds are clean; 2) report includes safe remediation guidance to classify stale vs actionable blockers and reconcile/clear them with audit trail; 3) docs/snippets that currently require source pulse-wrapper.sh plus list_active_worker_processes are replaced or supplemented with worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers or a dedicated no-source wrapper; 4) regression tests cover healthy runner + zero active workers + retained supervisor blockers.

## Why

Operational check on 2026-08-17 showed pulse looked healthy but logs still contained blocker debt. pulse-check-helper.sh report --since 24h --recent 24h --window 1h reported Active workers 0 / 2, available slots 2, queue 1 available / 8 open, GraphQL API OK remaining 4209/5000, runner HEALTHY, and Findings: None above thresholds. worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 7d reported 0 raw worker attempts and 0 terminal outcomes, but also 3 progress-blocker events, 2 proven current permission_required external_directory blockers from manual CLI sessions in a non-framework repo (private identifiers omitted), and 7 retained/unverified supervisor-pulse permission_required blockers from opencode-permission-broker. This is ambiguous for operators: there is no current worker failure, but retained blocker records remain unresolved and pulse-check hides them.

The same session found the documented/source-style diagnostic path is unsafe in OpenCode interactive command policy. A command using source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh plus list_active_worker_processes was blocked with dynamic shell control or launcher is unsupported: source. The safe command worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers returned 0.

## Files likely targets

- .agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh: retained-blocker advisory/reporting logic.
- .agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh: safe live-worker and blocker summary fields if needed.
- .agents/scripts/worker-blocker-* or blocker lifecycle helpers: retention/reconciliation semantics.
- .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md and .agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md / .agents/workflows/pulse.md: replace source-based worker-count snippets or mark them non-interactive-only.
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh and/or test-worker-activity-helper.sh: regression coverage.

## Implementation notes

Do not treat absent worker attempts as failed attempts. Keep private repo slugs, private issue titles, and local paths out of public output. Distinguish current actionable blockers from retained historical blockers. If stale-blocker cleanup is added, make it deterministic, bounded, tested, and auditable; do not silently delete evidence.

## Verification

Run .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh; .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh; .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh; ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report --since 7d --recent 24h --window 1h; ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers. Expected: runner can remain healthy, but pulse-check includes a retained supervisor permission-blocker advisory with redacted aggregate evidence and safe remediation guidance.

## Acceptance criteria

- Healthy idle pulse state remains healthy when there are no terminal failures.
- Retained/unverified supervisor permission blockers are visible in pulse-check output with safe next steps.
- Interactive-safe active-worker count path is documented and tested.
- Public output does not expose private repo slugs, private issue titles, or local/private paths.
- Regression tests cover the evidence shape above.

## Tier

tier:standard - bounded diagnostics/reporting change spanning pulse-check, blocker lifecycle semantics, docs, and privacy-safe output.

title: bug(session-miner): --create-issues dead — slug marcusquinn/aidevops not in repos.json, framework actuation never fires
body:
## Description

`session-miner-pulse.sh --create-issues` has never successfully fired on this instance. The actuation path requires `slug == "marcusquinn/aidevops"` with `role == "maintainer"` in `repos.json`, but no such entry exists — only `Majowka/*` repositories are registered. As a result, `framework_path` is always empty, the guard on line 1035 returns 1, and `_actuation_fingerprints` is never populated. Feedback candidates (instruction improvements, recurring error patterns) accumulate in `feedback_actions.md` indefinitely without ever being dispatched as issues.

## Expected Behavior

Session-miner should dispatch worker-ready issues to the appropriate framework repository when recurring error patterns or instruction candidates cross the confidence/frequency threshold, regardless of whether the local instance has `marcusquinn/aidevops` in `repos.json`. Either the slug check should be configurable, or the actuation target should fall back to a maintainer-role repo with a `framework: true` marker.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# session-miner-pulse.sh cron job (r-session-miner) — runs on schedule
# Equivalent manual check:
grep "marcusquinn/aidevops" ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json
```

**Actual output**:

```
(no output — slug not present)
```

**Cron lifecycle evidence**:

```json
{"timestamp":"2026-08-17T00:15:51Z","status":"failure","duration_seconds":476,...}
{"timestamp":"2026-08-17T02:07:57Z","status":"failure","duration_seconds":425,...}
```

Every session-miner cron run exits with `status: failure`. Feedback candidates are generated (11 action items, 5999 `bash:other` events flagged) but never dispatched.

**Expected output**:

Issues created in the target framework repo for recurring patterns above threshold.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `session-miner-pulse.sh:1031–1035` — `_create_issues_from_feedback()` function, guard block
- **Call chain**: cron job `r-session-miner` → `session-miner-pulse.sh --create-issues` → `_create_issues_from_feedback()` → `jq` filter on `repos.json` for `slug == "marcusquinn/aidevops"` → empty result → `return 1`
- **Integrated verification**: `grep "marcusquinn/aidevops" ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` returns no output; `lifecycle.jsonl` shows every run as `failure`

**Causal code**:

```bash
# session-miner-pulse.sh lines 1031–1035
framework_path=$(jq -r '
    [.initialized_repos[]? | select(.slug == "marcusquinn/aidevops" and .role == "maintainer")]
    | if length == 1 then .[0].path // "" else "" end
' "$REPOS_JSON" 2>/dev/null) || framework_path=""
[[ -n "$framework_path" && -d "$framework_path" ]] || return 1
```

**Call-site sweep**:

```
session-miner-pulse.sh:1032 — select(.slug == "marcusquinn/aidevops" and .role == "maintainer")
session-miner-pulse.sh:1036 — run_repo_scoped_pipeline ... "marcusquinn/aidevops"
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure `repos.json` contains only non-`marcusquinn/aidevops` entries (standard for non-framework-maintainer instances)
2. Run `session-miner-pulse.sh --create-issues`
3. Observe: no issues created, exit status 1 from `_create_issues_from_feedback`
4. Check `cron/r-session-miner/lifecycle.jsonl` — all entries show `"status":"failure"`

## Workarounds Applied

None applied — the failure was discovered through diagnostics. Manual review of `feedback_actions.md` is the only way to see candidates that should have been dispatched.

## Siblings

- `session-miner:bash:other` pattern — 5999 events flagged but never actioned (would be fixed by this issue resolving): See-also this issue
- `_SEVERITY_RANK` miscalibration — `bash:other` severity=low masks high-impact patterns: filed as sibling issue

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: mesh-manager (develop)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

title: bug(session-miner): bash:other severity hardcoded to low in _SEVERITY_RANK — 5999 terminal failures misclassified, never escalated
body:
## Description

`compress.py` classifies all `bash:other` errors as severity `low` via a static `_SEVERITY_RANK` dict. In practice, `bash:other` is the dominant error category (5999 events, 7 models) and the majority of these are OpenCode sandbox policy blocks (`BLOCKED by shared command policy`) — terminal failures that abort worker execution. The static classification means high-impact systemic failures are never escalated, never surface in priority triage, and their fix is perpetually deferred behind genuinely low-severity noise.

## Expected Behavior

Severity should reflect terminal impact. An error with `recovery: null` that halts a worker session is not equivalent to a recoverable warning. `bash:other` at scale (>1000 events, cross-model) should be classified `high` or `critical`, not `low`. The scoring formula should incorporate recovery rate and count thresholds, not just error category name.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
grep "_SEVERITY_RANK" ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/session-miner/compress.py
```

**Actual output**:

```python
_SEVERITY_RANK = {
    "permission": "high",
    "not_read_first": "high",
    "edit_stale_read": "medium",
    "edit_mismatch": "medium",
    "edit_multiple": "medium",
    "workdir_not_found": "medium",
    "file_not_found": "medium",
    "timeout": "low",
    "exit_code": "low",
    "other": "low",
}
```

**Observed impact**:

```
bash:other — count: 5999, models: 7, severity: low, score: 6020
```

(`feedback_actions.json` 2026-08-17T02:07:56Z)

All 5999 events are OpenCode sandbox `BLOCKED by shared command policy` — terminal failures that abort the bash tool call and leave the worker unable to proceed. Recovery rate from session-miner chunk data shows a significant portion with `recovery: null`.

**Expected output**:

`bash:other` with count >500 and cross-model scope classified `high`. Pattern with `recovery: null` majority classified `critical`.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `compress.py:194–205` — `_SEVERITY_RANK` dict, key `"other": "low"`
- **Call chain**: `session-miner-pulse.sh` → `compress_errors()` → `_build_error_patterns()` → `_SEVERITY_RANK.get(cat, "low")` → `severity` field in `feedback_actions.json`
- **Integrated verification**: `grep '"severity": "low"' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/session-miner/feedback_actions.json` returns `bash:other` with count 5999

**Causal code**:

```
compress.py lines 194–205: _SEVERITY_RANK dict — "other": "low"
compress.py line 248: severity=_SEVERITY_RANK.get(cat, "low")
```

**Call-site sweep**:

```
compress.py:248 — severity=_SEVERITY_RANK.get(cat, "low")
compress.py:194 — _SEVERITY_RANK dict definition (single location)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run session-miner pulse with active worker sessions that hit OpenCode sandbox blocks
2. Inspect `feedback_actions.json` — `bash:other` appears with thousands of events, `severity: low`
3. Compare to `bash:workdir_not_found` (8 events) = `severity: medium` — ordering is inverted

## Workarounds Applied

None. Issue discovered through manual review of `feedback_actions.json`.

## Siblings

- See-also: #30333 (session-miner actuation dead — severity misclassification prevents escalation even if actuation were fixed)
- See-also: bug filed for shell redirect contamination in framework prompts (root cause of bash:other volume)

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

Proposed fix: replace static dict with a two-axis classification — (1) category baseline severity + (2) volume/recovery override: if count >500 and cross-model → upgrade to `high`; if `recovery_null_rate > 0.5` → upgrade to `critical`. This keeps the dict for category baseline while adding runtime escalation for systemic patterns.

The `feedback_actions.json` `score` field (currently `count + model_count * ~3`) also does not reflect business impact. A terminal worker failure has higher cost than a recoverable one regardless of count.

title: bug(prompts): framework docs teach workers shell redirects blocked by OpenCode sandbox — worker-efficiency-protocol.md and shell-style-guide.md are primary vectors (5999 bash:other failures)
body:
## Description

46 files in `~/.aidevops/agents/` contain `2>/dev/null` in example code. Two of these files are loaded into every worker session context: `prompts/worker-efficiency-protocol.md` (seed prompt) and `reference/shell-style-guide.md`. The shell-style-guide explicitly labels `2>/dev/null || true` as an **"Allowed pattern"**. No rule anywhere warns workers that OpenCode sandbox blocks shell redirections, pipes, subshells, and process substitutions in Bash tool calls.

Workers learn these patterns in-context and generalize them — resulting in 5999 `bash:other` failures (7 models) from `BLOCKED by shared command policy` errors. The source of the blocking patterns is the framework's own documentation.

## Expected Behavior

- `worker-efficiency-protocol.md` and other worker-facing docs should contain zero redirect/pipe/subshell examples in Bash tool call contexts, or explicitly annotate them as "shell script only, not for Bash tool calls"
- `shell-style-guide.md` should distinguish between patterns valid in `.sh` scripts vs patterns valid in Bash tool calls
- AGENTS.md tool discipline section should include an explicit rule: "OpenCode Bash tool calls do not support shell redirections (`2>/dev/null`, `|`, `>`, `<(...)`, `$(subshell)`) — use separate sequential tool calls instead"

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
grep -rc "2>/dev/null" ~/.aidevops/agents/ | awk -F: '$2>0' | wc -l
```

**Actual output**:

```
46
```

**worker-efficiency-protocol.md lines 21 and 45** (seed prompt workers receive first):

```bash
# line 21 — PR creation example:
gh_issue=$(grep -E '^\s*- \[.\] <task-id> ' TODO.md 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'ref:GH#[0-9]+' | head -1 | sed 's/ref:GH#//' || true)

# line 45 — shellcheck example:
done < <(git diff --name-only origin/HEAD..HEAD 2>/dev/null | grep '\.sh$' || true)
```

**shell-style-guide.md line 134** — marked "Allowed pattern":

```bash
count=$(grep -c 'pat' file 2>/dev/null || true)
```

**Session-miner evidence** (`feedback_actions.json` 2026-08-17T02:07:56Z):

```
bash:other — count: 5999, models: 7, severity: low
```

Representative error from worker session (gh3897):

```
BLOCKED by shared command policy (forbid, command.parse-error): shell redirection is unsupported
bash: git ls-files 'backend/tests/**/*mqtt*' 'backend/tests/**/*import*' --cached 2>/dev/null
```

**Expected output**:

Worker uses `git ls-files 'backend/tests/**/*mqtt*'` without redirect. Or uses two sequential Bash tool calls.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `prompts/worker-efficiency-protocol.md:21,45` — loaded as part of worker seed context in every headless session
- **Call chain**: worker session start → framework docs loaded into context → model observes `2>/dev/null | pipe` patterns → model generalizes → Bash tool call with redirect → OpenCode sandbox `BLOCKED` → `bash:other` error recorded by session-miner
- **Integrated verification**: `grep -c "2>/dev/null" ~/.aidevops/agents/prompts/worker-efficiency-protocol.md` returns 2; session-miner `error_other_94.json` contains 117 records of `bash:other` from the same pattern across multiple sessions

**Call-site sweep** (top files by redirect count in worker-facing context):

```
prompts/worker-efficiency-protocol.md       2
reference/shell-style-guide.md              7 (2>/dev/null marked "allowed")
workflows/pulse-sweep.md                    4
workflows/pulse.md                          3
reference/dispatch-architecture.md          1
reference/worker-diagnostics.md             1
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a headless worker session for any issue
2. Worker reads `worker-efficiency-protocol.md` — sees `2>/dev/null | grep | head | sed` in PR creation example
3. Worker applies same pattern to a file discovery command
4. OpenCode sandbox blocks: `BLOCKED by shared command policy (forbid, command.parse-error): shell redirection is unsupported`
5. Worker session fails or degrades; `bash:other` recorded in session-miner

## Workarounds Applied

None applied in this session. Discovered through session-miner analysis and source reading.

## Siblings

- See-also: #30333 (session-miner actuation dead — these 5999 failures were never auto-dispatched)
- See-also: #30334 (severity miscalibration — these failures are classified low, never prioritized)

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

The fix is documentation-only — no runtime changes needed:

1. `prompts/worker-efficiency-protocol.md`: replace redirect examples with two-call patterns. Add bold note: "**Bash tool calls in OpenCode do not support redirections, pipes, or subshells — split into separate tool calls.**"
2. `reference/shell-style-guide.md`: add section header "Shell script context only" above patterns using `2>/dev/null`. Explicitly exclude Bash tool call context.
3. `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` tool discipline: add rule "Never use `2>/dev/null`, `|`, `>`, `<(...)`, or `$(subshell)` in Bash tool calls — OpenCode sandbox blocks these. Use the Grep tool or sequential Bash calls."

This is the highest-ROI fix in the set: one documentation change eliminates the primary source of worker session failures.

title: bug(prompts): unqualified templates/brief-template.md resolves to nonexistent worktree path — consolidation-task workers fail on Read (4 confirmed sessions)
body:
## Description

Framework documentation uses the unqualified path `templates/brief-template.md` in multiple reference files (`reference/task-lifecycle.md`, `reference/large-file-split.md`, `reference/task-taxonomy.md`, `workflows/plans.md`, `workflows/define.md`). When a worker resolves this path relative to its CWD (a linked worktree), it becomes `<worktree>/templates/brief-template.md` — a path that does not exist. The correct paths are either `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` (repo-local) or `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md` (framework global).

This affects consolidation-task workers and any worker that follows a `templates/brief-template.md` reference from a loaded framework doc.

## Expected Behavior

All references to the brief template in framework documentation should use fully-qualified paths that resolve correctly from a linked worktree CWD:
- For repo-local use: `.agents/templates/brief-template.md`
- For framework-global use: `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`

No unqualified `templates/brief-template.md` references should remain in worker-facing docs.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# Worker attempts to read brief template from worktree CWD:
# Read tool: templates/brief-template.md
# Resolved path (example worktree):
ls ~/Git/_worktrees/<repo>-<branch>/templates/brief-template.md
```

**Actual output**:

```
ls: cannot access '.../templates/brief-template.md': No such file or directory
```

**Session-miner evidence** (from `error_file_not_found_148.json`):

```
session: "Issue #3765: consolidation-task: merge thread on #3724 into single spec"
worktree: _worktrees/<repo>-feature-auto-<date>-gh3765
error: File not found: <worktree>/templates/brief-template.md
recovery: null
```

Same pattern confirmed in sessions gh3776, gh3779, gh3837.

**Causal reference** (example from `workflows/plans.md`):

```
Every task MUST have todo/tasks/{task_id}-brief.md. Use templates/brief-template.md.
```

Worker CWD = worktree root → resolves to `<worktree>/templates/brief-template.md` → ENOENT.

**Correct file locations**:

```bash
# Repo-local (correct):
ls .agents/templates/brief-template.md        # exists (git-tracked)
# Framework global (correct):
ls ~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md   # exists
# Wrong path workers hit:
ls <worktree>/templates/brief-template.md     # ENOENT
```

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `workflows/plans.md:81` — `Use templates/brief-template.md` (unqualified)
- **Call chain**: worker loads framework doc → reads `templates/brief-template.md` reference → attempts `Read` tool with relative path from worktree CWD → ENOENT → `file_not_found` error, `recovery: null`
- **Integrated verification**: session-miner `error_file_not_found_148.json` contains 4 confirmed instances across distinct sessions

**Call-site sweep** (unqualified references in framework docs):

```
reference/large-file-split.md:43
reference/task-taxonomy.md:121
reference/task-lifecycle.md:28
workflows/plans.md:81
workflows/define.md:15
workflows/optimize-tiers.md:84,118
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a consolidation-task worker to any worktree
2. Worker loads `workflows/plans.md` or `reference/task-lifecycle.md`
3. Worker attempts to read `templates/brief-template.md`
4. Read fails: path resolves to `<worktree>/templates/brief-template.md` which does not exist
5. `file_not_found` recorded, `recovery: null` — worker proceeds without brief template context

## Workarounds Applied

None applied. Discovered through session-miner `error_file_not_found` analysis.

## Siblings

- See-also: #30333 (session-miner actuation dead — these file_not_found events were never auto-dispatched as an issue)
- Bonus finding: `docs/developers/08-issue-briefs.md:321` declares "490 lines" for `brief-template.md` but current file has 168 lines — stale documentation

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

Fix: global search-and-replace `templates/brief-template.md` → `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md` in all worker-facing framework docs, or → `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` for repo-scoped docs. No runtime changes needed — documentation only.

No mechanism exists to copy framework files into worktrees on creation (by design — worktrees contain only git-tracked files). The fix must be at the reference level.

title: bug(headless-runtime-failure): hard_kill_stall with wait_status=0 misclassified as reason=clean — blocks ci-repair for CHANGES_REQUESTED PRs
body:
## Description

`classify_worker_exit` in `headless-runtime-failure.sh` emits `reason=clean` (or `reason=worker_noop_zero_output`) when a worker is killed by the watchdog (`hard_kill_stall`) but `wait_status=0`. This misclassification silently suppresses ci-repair dispatch for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs.

The root cause: `classify_worker_exit` (lines 663–696) handles `wait_status=0` by checking the OpenCode session DB and emitting `clean`/`worker_noop_zero_output` — but never inspects `.watchdog_stall_killed` / `.kill_reason` sentinels written by the watchdog. Those sentinels are only checked in the separate `classify_worker_kill_reason` function.

When the watchdog hard-kills a worker and `wait_status=0` happens to be the recorded status (GH#21707 context), the exit trap reads `wait_status=0` → enters the `"0"` branch → emits `clean`, bypassing the sentinel check entirely.

## Expected Behavior

When `.watchdog_stall_killed` or `.kill_reason` sentinels exist, `classify_worker_exit` should emit `hard_kill_stall` (or equivalent) regardless of `wait_status`. The sentinel files are ground truth for kill classification; `wait_status=0` should not override them.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (observed live on this instance):

```bash
cat ~/.aidevops-private/tmp/aidevops-headless-runtime.0CkOYx.kill_reason
# → hard_kill_stall

cat ~/.aidevops-private/tmp/aidevops-headless-runtime.0CkOYx.wait_status
# → 0
```

**Actual output** — worker outcome recorded as:

```
reason=clean
session_count=0
retry_class=unknown
```

**Expected output**:

```
reason=hard_kill_stall
retry_class=infrastructure_failure
```

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `headless-runtime-failure.sh:683` — `if [[ "$wait_status" == "0" ]]` branch in `classify_worker_exit`
- **Call chain**: EXIT trap → `classify_worker_exit "$exit_status"` → `wait_status=0` → branch at line 683 → no sentinel check → `printf 'clean'`
- **Integrated verification**: live sentinel files confirm the pattern on this instance — `aidevops-headless-runtime.0CkOYx.kill_reason=hard_kill_stall` AND `aidevops-headless-runtime.0CkOYx.wait_status=0` coexist; PR #3909 review-thread worker outcome (`reason=clean session_count=0`) matches the predicted misclassification exactly; `classify_worker_kill_reason` at line 780 correctly reads `.kill_reason` and `.watchdog_stall_killed` sentinels but is not called from the `wait_status=0` branch of `classify_worker_exit`

**Causal code**:

```bash
# headless-runtime-failure.sh lines 683-696
if [[ "$wait_status" == "0" ]]; then
    # ... checks opencode DB for session count ...
    printf '%s' "clean"   # ← emitted without checking kill sentinels
    return 0
fi
```

## Downstream Impact

The misclassification causes a cascade:

1. `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` records `reason=clean, session_count=0`
2. Scanner checks `outcome_reason == "worker_noop_zero_output"` to detect infrastructure failure (line 1347) — `clean` does not match → not classified as infrastructure
3. Scanner returns `PRRTS_RC_DISPATCH_DEFERRED` on repeated same-fingerprint with `analysis_complete=false`
4. `_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` returns `deferred`
5. `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` sets outcome=`deferred` → returns 1
6. `_review_gate_mode` stays `"merge"` (never becomes `"ci-rebase-only"`)
7. CI repair dispatch path (line 1613 of `pulse-merge.sh`) is never reached
8. PRs with `CHANGES_REQUESTED` + failing CI are permanently stuck — watchdog-killed review-thread worker blocks ci-repair

**Observed stuck PRs on this instance**: PRs with `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from reviewer citing CI failures, where the review-thread response worker was hard-killed, leaving ci-repair permanently blocked.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Worker is dispatched for review-thread response on a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PR
2. Worker stalls → watchdog writes `.watchdog_stall_killed` sentinel and kills with SIGKILL
3. Worker process exits; `wait_status=0` is recorded (GH#21707 pattern)
4. EXIT trap calls `classify_worker_exit "0"` → emits `clean`
5. `classify_worker_kill_reason` is called separately but its result is used only for metrics, not for outcome classification
6. Outcome written as `reason=clean, session_count=0`
7. Scanner misclassifies as non-infrastructure → deferred → blocks ci-repair

## Workarounds Applied

None. Identified through live analysis of stuck PRs and direct inspection of `.kill_reason` / `.wait_status` sentinel files.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

Related: GH#21707, GH#21818, GH#21754 — prior instances of `reason=clean` misclassification for killed workers.

**Proposed fix**: In `classify_worker_exit`, before the `wait_status=0` branch, check for `.watchdog_stall_killed` / `.kill_reason` sentinels via `classify_worker_kill_reason` and return the sentinel-derived reason if non-empty and non-`natural`. Alternatively, gate the `clean` emit on `classify_worker_kill_reason` returning `natural`.

```bash
# Proposed guard before line 683
local _kill_reason_check=""
_kill_reason_check=$(classify_worker_kill_reason "${_WORKER_EXIT_CODE_FILE:-}" "$wait_status")
if [[ "$_kill_reason_check" != "natural" && "$_kill_reason_check" != "unknown" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$_kill_reason_check"
    return 0
fi
```

title: t18293: Reject malformed GitHub login output before approval lifecycle mutation
body:
**Task ID:** `t18293` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~2h`
**Logged:** 2026-08-17
**Tags:** `bug` `security` `framework` `reliability` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Reject malformed GitHub login output before approval lifecycle mutation

## Done when

- [ ] A successful authenticated-user lookup returning one valid login passes exactly that login to the existing assignee mutation.
- [ ] A failed lookup that emits a GitHub HTTP 503 JSON body on stdout returns non-zero and performs no assignee mutation.
- [ ] Empty, multiline, whitespace-bearing, JSON, option-like, and control-character outputs cannot reach `--add-assignee`.
- [ ] Existing lifecycle lock fallback and `verify`/`reconcile` recovery semantics remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:696-714` — separate command success from output validation before assignment mutation.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-login-validation.sh` — hermetic success and malformed/error-output regressions.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_approval_apply_issue_lifecycle_updates()` consumes the authenticated login before `gh_issue_edit_safe --add-assignee`; no other caller was found in the scoped search.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `gh_issue_edit_safe` is the protected assignee mutation; status/label/lock mutations in the same lifecycle function must retain their current ordering and rollback behavior.
- **Tests/fixtures:** New focused shell test should source `approval-helper.sh`, stub `gh`, lifecycle helpers, and mutation calls; existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-rest-lock-fallback.sh` remains regression coverage.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because scoped search found no external schema or configuration for this internal login validation.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` later deploys `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`; do not edit `~/.aidevops/agents/` directly.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the change writes no persisted format and requires no historical backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Revert helper and focused test together; partial lifecycle recovery remains `aidevops approve verify` followed by `aidevops approve reconcile`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a small helper that runs `gh api user --jq '.login // empty'`, captures stdout only when the command exits successfully, rejects multiline or non-login-shaped output, prints only the validated login, and explicitly returns `0` or `1`.
2. Replace the `gh_user=$(... || printf '')` expression in `_approval_apply_issue_lifecycle_updates()` with fail-closed helper use. On failure, emit a concise diagnostic, do not call the assignee mutation, and return failure so existing recovery remains authoritative.
3. Add hermetic cases for a valid login, non-zero command with a JSON 503 body on stdout, empty output, multiline output, and punctuation/control-character payloads. Assert invalid payloads never appear in mutation arguments and no assignee mutation occurs.
4. Run focused shell tests, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint. Preserve Bash 3.2 syntax and explicit returns in every added function.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Validation happens before the assignee write; it must not introduce new state or race windows.
- **Migration/rollback:** No migration; reverting restores prior lookup behavior without changing stored data.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Accept legitimate GitHub/GitHub Enterprise login forms already handled by the repository; reject only values that cannot safely be one login argument.
- **Idempotency/retry:** A valid retry repeats existing idempotent lifecycle reconciliation; malformed output causes no new assignee write.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Earlier status/label work may already exist when lookup fails. Preserve the current non-zero result so `verify`/`reconcile` can inspect and complete the lifecycle later.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-login-validation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-rest-lock-fallback.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-login-validation.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** The focused test proves valid forwarding and malformed-output rejection; REST-lock coverage proves lifecycle recovery is preserved; ShellCheck/lint cover Bash portability and repository policy.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required unless implementation changes shared GitHub wrappers outside the declared scope.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** Prevent malformed GitHub identity output from becoming an assignee mutation.
- **Preserved user directions:** Solve this independently from batch outage circuit-breaking.
- **Trigger and evidence:** Historical HTTP 503 outage recovered before issue publication; no active safety stop.

title: bug(pulse-merge-stuck): CHANGES_REQUESTED early-return in _pms_is_eligible_stuck blinds broken-base pattern outage detection
body:
## Description

`_pms_is_eligible_stuck()` in `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` returns `0` (not stuck) for
any PR with `reviewDecision == CHANGES_REQUESTED`. This causes those PRs to be
excluded from `eligible_stuck_count`, which is the only input to
`_detect_pattern_outage`. When multiple worker PRs share an identical CI failure
fingerprint from a broken base branch, no pattern-outage issue is ever filed —
because all such PRs have `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (set by the OCR review bot after
CI fails), and none of them reach the pattern-outage grouping step.

## Expected Behavior

Worker PRs that have `CHANGES_REQUESTED` **exclusively because CI is failing**
(not because of substantive review objections) should be eligible for
`_detect_pattern_outage` when they share an identical CI failure fingerprint with
≥ `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_PATTERN_MIN_PRS` (default: 3) other PRs. A pattern-outage
issue should be filed pointing at the broken base branch.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
gh issue list --repo Majowka/mesh-manager --state open --label "pattern-outage" --limit 10
```

**Actual output**:

```
[]
```

No pattern-outage issue, despite 4 open worker PRs all failing the exact same check:

| PR | Title | Failing check | reviewDecision |
|----|-------|---------------|----------------|
| #3958 | fix(backend): asyncio deprecation | `🧪 backend - real-integration-2` | CHANGES_REQUESTED |
| #3939 | fix(commands): gate dispatch | `🧪 backend - real-integration-2` | CHANGES_REQUESTED |
| #3909 | fix(bridges): update_config | `🧪 backend - real-integration-2` | CHANGES_REQUESTED |
| #3954 | chore(ci): bump trivy-action | `🧪 backend - real-integration-2` | CHANGES_REQUESTED |

All 4 PRs fail an identical test: `test_deployment_start_pause_resume_real`
(resume returns 404 — a regression in `develop`, not in the PRs themselves).
`AIDEVOPS_MERGE_PATTERN_MIN_PRS=3` threshold met (4 ≥ 3), but no outage issue.

**Expected output:** a `pattern-outage` issue filed against `Majowka/mesh-manager`
indicating that `🧪 backend - real-integration-2` / `📊 Quality Gates` is a
broken-base regression affecting ≥ 4 worker PRs.

**Causal status:** confirmed

**Owning-path proof:**

- **Production entry point**: `pulse_merge_stuck_run_pass()` —
  `pulse-merge-stuck.sh:1632` — called by `pulse-wrapper.sh` on each cycle.
- **Call chain**:
  1. `pulse_merge_stuck_run_pass` → `_pms_classify_pr_list` (~line 1660)
  2. Per-PR loop: `_pms_is_eligible_stuck "$pr_obj"` — `pulse-merge-stuck.sh:1608`
  3. `_pms_is_eligible_stuck` early-returns `0` at line 217–221 for `CHANGES_REQUESTED`
  4. PR is never added to `eligible_stuck_count` or `stuck_pr_numbers`
  5. `eligible_stuck_count` stays at 0 → guard at line 1714 never passes →
     `_detect_pattern_outage` is never called
- **Integrated verification**: `tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh` — no test
  covers the case where `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs with identical CI fingerprints
  should trigger pattern outage (tests only cover `APPROVED + MERGEABLE` path).

**Causal code:**

```bash
# pulse-merge-stuck.sh:217-221
# CHANGES_REQUESTED is a real review block, not a stuck state
[[ "$review_decision" == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" ]] && {
    printf '0'
    return 0
}
```

```bash
# pulse-merge-stuck.sh:1714-1716 — never reached for CHANGES_REQUESTED PRs
if [[ "$eligible_stuck_count" -ge "$AIDEVOPS_MERGE_PATTERN_MIN_PRS" ]]; then
    _detect_pattern_outage "$repo_slug" "$(printf '%b' "$stuck_pr_numbers")" "$pr_json" || true
fi
```

**Call-site sweep:**

```
pulse-merge-stuck.sh:199     _pms_is_eligible_stuck()  — definition
pulse-merge-stuck.sh:1608    is_stuck=$(_pms_is_eligible_stuck "$pr_obj")  — only call site
```

## Proposed Fix

Separate the eligibility for **individual PR escalation** (which correctly excludes
`CHANGES_REQUESTED`) from eligibility for **pattern-outage fingerprint grouping**
(which should include `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs if their failure is CI-only).

Option A — add a dedicated `_pms_is_pattern_outage_eligible()` predicate that
returns `1` for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs with at least one terminal CI failure,
and feed its output into a parallel fingerprint-collection loop in
`_detect_pattern_outage`.

Option B — pass `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs through to `_detect_pattern_outage`
unconditionally and let `_pms_is_per_pr_gate_fingerprint()` filter out
review-policy-only fingerprints (LGTM/approval checks) versus shared CI checks.

Option B is lower surface-area: the per-PR gate fingerprint filter already exists
at `pulse-merge-stuck.sh:764` and would correctly suppress review-decision gates
(`reviewDecision`, `status:approved`, etc.) while passing through shared CI
check fingerprints.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have ≥ 3 open worker PRs (`origin:worker`) in a managed repo all failing the
   same required CI check.
2. Ensure the CI failure originates from `develop` (not from the PR diff).
3. OCR review bot or senior reviewer sets `CHANGES_REQUESTED` on each PR citing
   the CI failure.
4. Wait for `pulse_merge_stuck_run_pass` to execute.
5. Observe: no `pattern-outage` issue is filed; `eligible_stuck_count=0` in pulse.log.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manual inspection of CI failure across all open PRs to identify shared
  `test_deployment_start_pause_resume_real` failure in `develop`.
- Filed this issue manually to surface the broken-base regression.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)
- **Working repo**: mesh-manager (develop)

## Additional Context

The comment at `pulse-merge-stuck.sh:217` — `"CHANGES_REQUESTED is a real review
block, not a stuck state"` — is correct for individual PR escalation purposes.
The design intent is sound. The gap is that this correct individual-escalation
guard also prevents the batch pattern-outage path from seeing CI-failed
`CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs, which was likely not the intended consequence when
`_detect_pattern_outage` was added.

Siblings filed in same session:
- See-also: (stall detector for origin:worker CI-red PRs — sibling #2)
- See-also: (worker prompt scope boundary missing — sibling #3)

title: bug(pulse): no stall detector for origin:worker CI-red PRs with no new commits — stalled worker sessions leave PRs unremediated
body:
## Description

There is no pulse mechanism that detects `origin:worker` PRs which have:
- failing CI (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` from review bot citing CI failure), AND
- no new commits for > 24 hours, AND
- no active worker process linked to the PR.

When a headless worker session ends after producing a failing PR but cannot fix
the CI failure (e.g., because the failure originates in `develop`), the PR
remains open indefinitely with no redispatch. Existing sweepers do not cover
this case:

- `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` — handles only `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"` (merge
  conflicts), not CI-red PRs.
- `cleanup_stalled_workers` in `pulse-cleanup.sh:710` — detects only live
  processes by log size; a finished worker leaves no live process to detect.
- `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` — explicitly excludes `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PRs from
  eligible-stuck classification (`pulse-merge-stuck.sh:217-221`), so it never
  fires for these PRs.
- `pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` — handles triage/routine/FOSS dispatch, not
  worker-PR no-activity recovery.

## Expected Behavior

Pulse should detect `origin:worker` + `status:in-review` PRs where:
- CI is failing (at least one required check has `FAILURE` conclusion), AND
- `updatedAt` is older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 24 h), AND
- no active headless worker session is linked to the PR.

And either:
1. Redispatch a repair worker against the linked issue, OR
2. Escalate via the existing individual-PR escalation path in
   `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (`_escalate_individual_stuck_pr`).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
gh pr view 3923 --repo Majowka/mesh-manager --json number,title,updatedAt,reviewDecision,labels
```

**Actual output**:

```json
{
  "number": 3923,
  "title": "feat(frontend): add i18n coverage to Dashboard page (Resolves #3888)",
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-14T18:03:19Z",
  "reviewDecision": "CHANGES_REQUESTED",
  "labels": [{"name": "status:in-review"}, {"name": "origin:worker"}]
}
```

PR open since 2026-08-14 (3+ days as of 2026-08-17). CI failing
(`frontend - unit`, `frontend - integration`). No new commits since last worker
session. No active worker. No redispatch.

**Expected output:** a repair worker dispatched against issue #3888, OR an
escalation issue filed.

**Causal status:** confirmed — gap in coverage, not a regression.

**Owning-path proof:**

- **Production entry point**: `pulse_merge_stuck_run_pass()` and
  `dirty_pr_sweep_all_repos()` — the two periodic PR-state sweepers in the
  pulse cycle.
- **Call chain**: neither sweeper processes the `origin:worker` + CI-red +
  no-activity case. `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:1260` filters to `mergeStateStatus
  == "DIRTY"` only. `pulse-merge-stuck.sh:217-221` returns 0 for
  `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
- **Integrated verification**: no existing test covers this recovery path.
  `ls ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-open-pr-sweep.sh` → not found.
  `ls ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-stalled-pr-sweep.sh` → not found.

**Call-site sweep:**

```
pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:1260   filters to DIRTY only
pulse-merge-stuck.sh:217-221   returns 0 for CHANGES_REQUESTED
pulse-cleanup.sh:710           cleanup_stalled_workers() — live processes only
```

## Proposed Fix

Add a new periodic sweep (e.g., `pulse-stalled-worker-pr-sweep.sh`) or extend
`pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` with a CI-red + no-activity lane:

```
for each open PR with origin:worker + status:in-review:
  if updatedAt older than STALLED_WORKER_PR_AGE_HOURS (default 24h):
    if any required CI check has FAILURE:
      if no active worker session owns this PR:
        → route linked issue for redispatch via _transition_issue_for_redispatch
```

The active-worker ownership check can use the existing dispatch-ledger
(`dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`) keyed by repo + PR number.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a headless worker against an issue.
2. Worker produces a PR with failing CI (e.g., because `develop` is broken).
3. Worker session ends normally (exits after PR creation).
4. Wait > 24 hours.
5. Observe: PR sits open with no new commits and no redispatch.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manual identification of stalled PR via `gh pr list` audit.
- Reported to interactive session for human follow-up.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode

title: bug(pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt): _dlw_first_pass_completion_contract lacks scope boundary — workers silently expand to out-of-brief files
body:
## Description

`_dlw_first_pass_completion_contract()` in `pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`
(lines 326–338) is injected into every worker prompt via three paths (clean-room,
zero-output fallback, and normal). It does not contain a scope boundary
instruction. Point 2 of the contract actively broadens scope:

> "Treat prior structured CI/review feedback in the issue body as cumulative
> evidence. Address **every** terminal failing check, including advisory checks,
> not only the first required failure."

"Every terminal failing check" without a file-scope guard allows workers to fix
files unrelated to the brief's stated targets when CI failures reference those
files. This produces PRs that carry undisclosed changes outside the stated scope,
which: (a) forces maintainers to re-review unrelated logic, (b) triggers
additional `CHANGES_REQUESTED` rounds, and (c) stalls merge.

The pattern has been observed 4 times in the same managed repository session
(PRs #3879, #3947, #3939, #3957 in `Majowka/mesh-manager`), all touching
`backend/app/services/bulk_deployment_service.py` despite none of the
corresponding issues mentioning that file. The same pattern is documented in the
repository's own `tasks/lessons.md:28-34`:

> Worker changed `approval.py` as an incidental side-effect of removing
> `notify_system_event` from `websocket.py` (the primary target). The brief
> listed only `socketio_service.py` and `websocket.py`.

## Expected Behavior

Workers should modify only files explicitly declared in the brief's `EDIT:`,
`NEW:`, or `File:` scope. If a terminal CI failure requires changing a file
outside that scope, the worker should stop and report a blocker rather than
silently expanding scope.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
gh pr view 3957 --repo Majowka/mesh-manager --json title,files
```

**Actual output** (abridged):

```json
{
  "title": "feat(bridge): per-bridge capability gating at service layer (Resolves #3945)",
  "files": [
    "backend/app/bridge/schemas/bridge/commands.py",
    "backend/app/bridge/api/commands.py",
    "backend/app/bridge/services/command_service.py",
    "backend/app/services/bulk_deployment_service.py",
    "backend/tests/integration/real/test_deployment_lifecycle_real.py",
    "backend/tests/unit/services/test_bulk_deployment_service.py"
  ]
}
```

Issue #3945 brief described only the capability-gate files (commands.py,
command_service.py, test files for those). `bulk_deployment_service.py` and
`test_deployment_lifecycle_real.py` are not mentioned. Senior reviewer
(@kamcio2603) flagged this as "4th occurrence of the same smuggled-scope
anti-pattern this session".

**Expected output:** PR contains only files listed in the #3945 brief.

**Causal status:** confirmed

**Owning-path proof:**

- **Production entry point**: `_dlw_prepare_prompt_for_launch()` —
  `pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh:396` — called by `dispatch_with_dedup` for
  every worker launch.
- **Call chain**:
  1. `dispatch_with_dedup` → `_dlw_prepare_prompt_for_launch`
  2. All three prompt paths (clean-room :430, zero-output :449, normal :455)
     append `_dlw_first_pass_completion_contract`
  3. Contract point 2 instructs worker to fix "every terminal failing check"
     without scope restriction
  4. Worker reads CI failure output → finds `bulk_deployment_service.py` in
     stack trace → treats it as in-scope
- **Integrated verification**: `tasks/lessons.md:28-34` in managed repo
  documents the identical pattern as a prior confirmed incident.

**Causal code:**

```bash
# pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh:331
2. Treat prior structured CI/review feedback in the issue body as cumulative
evidence. Address every terminal failing check, including advisory checks,
not only the first required failure.
```

No scope-boundary point exists in the 6-point contract.

**Call-site sweep:**

```
pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh:430   _dlw_first_pass_completion_contract (clean-room path)
pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh:449   _dlw_first_pass_completion_contract (zero-output path)
pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh:455   _dlw_first_pass_completion_contract (normal path)
```

## Proposed Fix

Insert a scope-boundary point after point 3 in `_dlw_first_pass_completion_contract`:

```text
3a. Scope boundary: modify only files explicitly declared as EDIT:, NEW:, or
File: targets in the worker brief. Do not fix, refactor, reformat, or add
changes in files outside that scope because of incidental CI or review findings.
If a terminal failing check requires an out-of-scope file change, stop and report
a blocker with the failing command, affected path, and reason; request a revised
brief or create a follow-up child issue rather than expanding scope silently.
```

This does not prevent workers from reading context files — only from writing to
files outside the declared scope.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a worker against an issue whose brief lists specific target files.
2. The repo has a CI failure that involves a file not listed in the brief.
3. Worker reads CI output, sees the unlisted file in a stack trace.
4. Worker modifies both the brief's targets and the unlisted file.
5. PR reviewer flags undisclosed scope change; CHANGES_REQUESTED issued.

## Workarounds Applied

None automated. Each occurrence required manual senior review to detect and
flag. Worker must be redispatched to strip out-of-scope changes.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.269
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

See-also: #30348 (CHANGES_REQUESTED blind-spot in pattern-outage detection —
primary issue in the same investigation session).

The `pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` script checks declared brief target file
sizes before dispatch but does not compare actual post-dispatch `git diff
--name-only` against the brief's allowlist. A complementary post-commit gate
(pre-push hook or CI check) that compares diff paths to the issue brief's `EDIT:`
declarations would close the gap structurally.

title: Route stalled Dependabot PRs through trusted merge or worker repair
body:
Problem: Dependabot PRs can remain open indefinitely because the merge pass rejects the bot as a non-collaborator before repair routing. The narrow trusted path depends on a static package allowlist; PRs outside it receive no CodeRabbit review, have no linked issue, and cannot enter the existing worker feedback router. Observed on open PRs #30034-#30039. Root cause: .agents/scripts/trusted-dependabot-lib.sh requires explicit historical dependency entries; .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh runs the external-author gate before CI repair routing; .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh::_route_pr_to_fix_worker requires a linked worker issue and rejects unowned bot PRs; the review-bot gate remains a terminal WAITING state. Required outcome: preserve exact-head GitHub Bot identity, same-repository ownership, bot-authored commits, file-scope, security checks, and CI fail-closed boundaries; automatically progress safe Dependabot dependency updates without per-package allowlist churn; convert non-green or policy-ineligible Dependabot PRs into an idempotent worker-ready repair or triage path; add observability distinguishing trusted merge, worker routing, and maintainer hold. Files: .agents/scripts/trusted-dependabot-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh, .agents/configs/trusted-dependabot-updates.conf, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-trusted-dependabot.sh, plus focused routing coverage. Verification: trusted Dependabot tests, new routing tests, ShellCheck changed scripts, relevant local framework lint gates, and current-PR classification evidence.

body:

This creates a false-green regression gate. ## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #30370)

The previous worker's PR #30370 (`GH#30357: repair trusted @types/bun dependency update`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (4 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/configs/trusted-dependabot-updates.conf
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-trusted-dependabot.sh
bun.lock
package.json
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `bdca60a199a66784ca7ff48ba913faec1866c047`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/30370/head:recovered-30370
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick bdca60a199a66784ca7ff48ba913faec1866c047
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #30370's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`.

_Routed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)._

title: Prevent concurrent duplicate Dependabot intake issues
body:
## Problem

After v3.32.270 deployed the GH#30351 Dependabot intake route, overlapping Pulse processes created multiple worker issues for the same PR despite the pre-create marker search. Observed duplicates: PR #30038 produced #30357/#30358; #30037 produced #30359/#30360; #30036 produced #30361/#30362/#30363; #30035 produced #30364/#30365/#30366; #30034 produced #30367/#30368.

## Root cause hypothesis

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` uses a search-then-create sequence without concurrency serialization or post-create reconciliation, so overlapping processes can both observe no marker and create an issue.

## Implementation

- Modify `.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` to guarantee convergence to one canonical open issue per repository/PR marker under concurrent invocations.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` with deterministic concurrent-creation coverage.
- Preserve fail-closed Bot identity checks, dry-run no-write behavior, wrapper-created issue metadata, and worker dispatchability.
- Reconcile the observed duplicate issues by retaining one canonical issue per PR and closing superseded copies with a concise reference.

## Verification

- Run the Dependabot intake test suite including a concurrent invocation test.
- Run ShellCheck on changed shell files and `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`.
- Exercise the deployed route and verify exactly one open marker issue remains per affected Dependabot PR.

title: Route authentic Dependabot PRs with paginated check rollups
body:
## Problem

The deployed GH#30351 worker-intake route still skips authentic Dependabot PRs when their status-check rollup exceeds 100 entries. PR #30039 currently has 109 check contexts after repeated runs, so the shared full trust snapshot rejects it as paginated before worker-intake authentication can run.

## Reproducer

1. Use an authentic same-repository Dependabot PR with a Dependabot-authored exact head and more than 100 status-check contexts.
2. Run the deployed Pulse merge pass.
3. Observe `Merge pass: skipping PR ... author app/dependabot is not a collaborator` instead of worker intake.

Live evidence: PR #30039 has one Dependabot-authored commit, 22 changed files, and 109 status-check entries. Pulse logged the collaborator skip at `2026-08-17T23:20:49Z` after v3.32.271 deployed.

## Implementation

- Modify `.agents/scripts/trusted-dependabot-lib.sh` so worker-intake authentication can verify Bot identity, same-repository ownership, exact head, and complete commit authorship without requiring a complete files/checks snapshot.
- Keep automatic merge trust fail-closed when files or checks are paginated.
- Reuse the full exact-head snapshot when available and use a bounded authentication-only fallback only when it is unavailable.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-trusted-dependabot.sh` and intake coverage for the paginated-check fallback.

## Verification

- Run trusted Dependabot and intake suites, ShellCheck, and `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`.
- Publish through the authorized patch-release flow.
- Verify PR #30039 routes to exactly one open worker issue rather than the collaborator skip.

title: Stop Dependabot intake recreation after maintainer hold
body:
## Problem

Pulse recreates a Dependabot worker-intake issue after a worker explicitly places the source PR on maintainer review and closes the prior intake issue. PR #30039 is intentionally held with `needs-maintainer-review`; issue #30387 recorded the hold and closed, then Pulse created duplicate issue #30388 eleven minutes later.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

`gh issue list --repo <owner/repo> --state all --search '"Dependabot PR #30039 requires worker resolution" in:title'`

**Actual output:** closed intake issues #30356 and #30387 are followed by open issue #30388 while source PR #30039 remains explicitly held with `needs-maintainer-review`.

**Expected output:** once an authentic Dependabot PR carries a live maintainer-review hold, Pulse preserves that PR without creating another worker-intake issue.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` deduplicates only against open intake issues and does not inspect the source PR's live hold state before creating a replacement issue.

## Implementation

- Make the intake route detect a live `needs-maintainer-review` label on the authenticated source PR and return a distinct held outcome without writing an issue.
- Keep authentication fail-closed and make unavailable PR-label evidence fail closed rather than creating work.
- Preserve current open-issue idempotency, concurrent locking, dry-run behavior, and automatic-merge trust boundaries.
- Add focused regression tests and caller logging for the held outcome.

## Verification

- Run Dependabot intake, trusted-snapshot, and merge-routing tests plus ShellCheck and local linters.
- Exercise the live held PR #30039 and verify no replacement intake issue is created.
- Close #30388 as superseded after the fix is deployed, then publish the authorized patch release.

title: bug: CHANGES_REQUESTED_THREAD_REMEDIATION_FIRST=1 creates infinite merge-skip loop when scanner reaches same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint escalation
body:
## Description

When `AIDEVOPS_CHANGES_REQUESTED_THREAD_REMEDIATION_FIRST=1`, a worker PR stuck on `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` enters an infinite merge-skip loop if the `pr-review-thread-response-scanner` reaches its `same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint` escalation threshold. The PR is skipped on every merge pass with no recovery path — it never gets routed to a fix worker.

Observed in production: PR Majowka/mesh-manager#3923 has been stuck for 4+ days with hundreds of `pw-merge-skip-changes-requested` log events and zero routing activity.

## Expected Behavior

After the thread remediation path exhausts its retry budget (`same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint` after N attempts), control should fall through to `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` so a fix worker can address the review feedback and open a new PR.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr 3923 --repo Majowka/mesh-manager
```

**Actual output**:

```
pw-merge-skip-changes-requested: Merge pass skipped — review decision is CHANGES_REQUESTED
(repeated 200+ times, no routing events)

Ancillary workers:
  thread-response  attempt=3  outcome=
    blocked_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint
```

**Expected output**: After attempt=3 with same fingerprint, PR should be routed to fix worker (`_dispatch_pr_fix_worker`) and closed so the issue re-enters the dispatch queue.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-merge.sh:1552` — merge cycle evaluates `if [[ "$pr_review" == "$_changes_requested" ]]` and enters the CHANGES_REQUESTED gate
- **Call chain**: `_process_single_ready_pr:1552` → `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate:1560` → `_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation:357` → scanner escalates after attempt=3 same fingerprint → `PRRTS_RC_MAINTAINER_ATTENTION` returned → `_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` sets `outcome="maintainer_attention"` and returns **0** (`pulse-merge.sh:149-152`) → `if` block at `pulse-merge.sh:351` fires → `return 1` at line 370 → **`_route_pr_to_fix_worker` at line 376 never reached**
- **Integrated verification**: `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr 3923 --repo Majowka/mesh-manager` shows 200+ `pw-merge-skip-changes-requested` events with zero `pw-review-route-*` events; ancillary worker state shows `attempt=3, blocked_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint`

**Causal code**:

```bash
# pulse-merge.sh:351-384
if _pulse_merge_changes_requested_thread_remediation_first_enabled \
    && [[ ... origin:worker ... ]] \
    && _pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation "$pr_number" "$repo_slug" "after CHANGES_REQUESTED review gate"; then
    if [[ "$_PULSE_MERGE_REMEDIATION_OUTCOME" == "maintainer_attention" ]]; then
        echo "...terminal review-thread maintainer attention pending, preserving PR..."
    fi
    return 1   # ← BUG: always returns here when remediation returns 0, including maintainer_attention
fi
# _route_pr_to_fix_worker is here — NEVER REACHED when maintainer_attention outcome
_route_pr_to_fix_worker "$pr_number" "$repo_slug" "$linked_issue" "review" "$_cr_pr_labels" || review_route_rc=$?
```

**Call-site sweep**:

```bash
grep -n "maintainer_attention\|PULSE_REVIEW_REMEDIATION_MAINTAINER_ATTENTION_RC" \
  ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
# pulse-merge.sh:77:  PULSE_REVIEW_REMEDIATION_MAINTAINER_ATTENTION_RC=12
# pulse-merge.sh:149: if [[ "$scanner_rc" -eq "$PULSE_REVIEW_REMEDIATION_MAINTAINER_ATTENTION_RC" ]]
# pulse-merge.sh:365: elif [[ "$_PULSE_MERGE_REMEDIATION_OUTCOME" == "maintainer_attention" ]]
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable `AIDEVOPS_CHANGES_REQUESTED_THREAD_REMEDIATION_FIRST=1`
2. Have an `origin:worker` PR with `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` whose review thread cannot be resolved by the ancillary worker (e.g., reviewer said "fix CI first" — no inline threads to resolve)
3. Wait for `_prrts_should_escalate_attempt` threshold (default: 3 same-fingerprint attempts with same head SHA)
4. Observe: merge pass skips the PR every cycle indefinitely with no fix-worker routing

## Proposed Fix

In `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` (`pulse-merge.sh:351-384`), the `maintainer_attention` outcome should NOT prevent fallthrough to `_route_pr_to_fix_worker`. Options:

**Option A** (minimal): When `_PULSE_MERGE_REMEDIATION_OUTCOME == "maintainer_attention"` AND the root cause is `same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint`, return 1 from `_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` (scanner RC 12 → treat as failure, not success) so the `if` block doesn't fire and `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` is reached.

**Option B** (explicit): Inside the `maintainer_attention` branch of `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate`, explicitly call `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` before `return 1`.

Option A is less invasive. The design intent of `MAINTAINER_ATTENTION_RC` is "this path needs human intervention" — but for `same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint` specifically, a fresh fix worker (which will re-read the review and address the actual feedback) is the correct automated response.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually change issue #3888 label from `status:in-review` → `status:available` to allow re-dispatch after confirming this loop

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.273
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21
- `AIDEVOPS_CHANGES_REQUESTED_THREAD_REMEDIATION_FIRST=1` (set in `~/.config/aidevops/tenants/default/credentials.sh:11`)
- Affected PR: Majowka/mesh-manager#3923 (4+ days stuck)
- Affected files: `pulse-merge.sh:351-384`, `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:210-220,2479-2491`

## Additional Context

Issue #26535 (`_handle_changes_requested_review_gate skips thread remediation`) was the inverse problem — remediation wasn't being called at all. That fix introduced `CHANGES_REQUESTED_THREAD_REMEDIATION_FIRST`. This issue is the follow-on: remediation IS called but produces a terminal outcome (`maintainer_attention`) that prevents the existing fix-worker fallback from firing.

The `same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint` escalation (`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:218`) is correct — after 3 attempts with identical thread state it correctly gives up on ancillary workers. The bug is solely in `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` not distinguishing between "remediation actively working" (deferred/queued → preserve PR) and "remediation exhausted" (maintainer_attention from same_unresolved → fall through to fix worker).

title: bug: ready_missing_summary skips status:in-review transition, stale scan resets issue to status:available creating re-dispatch risk on open approved PR
body:
## Description

When a worker creates a PR using raw `gh pr create` (without posting a `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` comment to the PR), the runtime classifies the worker's output as `ready_missing_summary`. This causes `_hrw_finish_success_run` to set `release_needed=0`, skipping `_release_dispatch_claim` entirely. No `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment is posted. The linked issue is never transitioned to `status:in-review`.

Later, the stale-assignment scan (`pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`) detects an issue with `status:in-progress` and no live worker process, and resets it to `status:available`. The issue now appears as a fresh dispatch target despite having an open, approved PR — creating a re-dispatch risk that would produce a competing duplicate PR on top of an already-approved one.

Observed in production: issue Majowka/mesh-manager#3896, worker session `ses_fee0334f4ffeVitjfsyGv8Cs2D` (PID 2195347, attempt `cb3384d2-c6c1-4465-adf3-0918f57b167b`). PR Majowka/mesh-manager#3964 was created and subsequently APPROVED, but the issue has `status:available` and is re-dispatch eligible.

## Expected Behavior

When a worker creates a PR (even without a MERGE_SUMMARY comment), the linked issue should transition to `status:in-review` so the issue is NOT re-dispatched until the PR is merged, closed, or explicitly re-queued. Either:
- `ready_missing_summary` should still execute `status:in-review` transition before retaining the claim, OR
- The stale scan should detect an existing open PR linked to the issue before resetting to `status:available`

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
tail -5 /run/user/1000/aidevops/pulse/pulse-Majowka-mesh-manager-3896.log
```

**Actual output**:

```
[INFO]  [lifecycle] worker_failure_evidence session=issue-3896 result=success exit_code=0 kill_reason=natural launch_failure_cause=none next_action=none
[WARNING] [lifecycle] worker_ready_missing_summary session=issue-3896 — protected/inconclusive PR state is not completion evidence; retaining claim
```

Then, minutes later, stale scan resets issue:

```
gh issue view 3896 --repo Majowka/mesh-manager --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name]'
# → ["status:available","origin:interactive","tier:standard","auto-dispatch"]
# Expected: ["status:in-review","origin:interactive","tier:standard","auto-dispatch"]
```

**Expected output**: `status:in-review` on the issue after worker exit. No re-dispatch while PR is open.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `headless-runtime-worker.sh:1902` — case statement in `_hrw_finish_success_run` evaluating `output_class` returned by `_worker_produced_output`
- **Call chain**: worker opencode exits with code 0 → `_cmd_run_finish` → `_hrw_finish_success_run:1847` → `_worker_produced_output` returns `"ready_missing_summary"` because PR exists (`gh pr view` confirms open PR) but no `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` comment found in PR comments → `case ready_missing_summary` at `headless-runtime-worker.sh:1902` → `release_needed=0` → `_hrw_release_dispatch_claim` NOT called → no `CLAIM_RELEASED` posted → no `status:in-review` set → issue stays `status:in-progress` → stale scan (`pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:50`) detects abandoned `status:in-progress` + assignee + no live process → calls `set_issue_status ... "available"` → issue is now `status:available` with open approved PR
- **Integrated verification**: `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` entry for session `issue-3896` shows `result=success,exit_code=0,kill_reason=natural` while issue simultaneously has `status:available` and zero `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment in issue #3896 GitHub thread; PR #3964 open + approved

**Causal code**:

```bash
# headless-runtime-worker.sh:1902-1907
protected_draft | unverified_open_pr | head_mismatch | ready_missing_summary | merged_missing_summary)
    local noncomplete_reason="worker_${output_class}"
    print_warning "[lifecycle] ${noncomplete_reason} session=${session_key} — protected/inconclusive PR state is not completion evidence; retaining claim"
    release_needed=0
    _hrw_mark_failed_terminal_state "$_HRW_STATUS_FAILED" "$noncomplete_reason"
    ;;
# Note: no status:in-review transition, no CLAIM_RELEASED — issue left in status:in-progress
# which stale scan later resets to status:available (pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:50)
```

**Call-site sweep**:

```bash
grep -n "ready_missing_summary\|release_needed=0" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh
# 539: "ready_missing_summary" — exact-head ready PR lacks MERGE_SUMMARY
# 1902: protected_draft | unverified_open_pr | head_mismatch | ready_missing_summary | ...
# 1905: release_needed=0
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a worker to an issue in a repo
2. Worker creates a PR using raw `gh pr create --body-file ...` (without calling aidevops full-loop helpers that post the MERGE_SUMMARY comment)
3. Worker's opencode session ends with exit_code=0 (natural session limit or `stop`)
4. Observe: worker log ends with `worker_ready_missing_summary ... retaining claim`
5. Observe: no `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment posted to issue
6. Wait for stale scan interval (default TTL)
7. Observe: issue transitions to `status:available` despite open PR

## Root Cause Analysis

The worker session (`ses_fee0334f4ffeVitjfsyGv8Cs2D`) ran for exactly 1800s (session time limit). Session log shows it committed the fix, pushed the branch, and called `gh pr create --body-file ...` at `ts=1787009464` — approximately 90 seconds before the 30-minute limit. The session exited cleanly via opencode `reason=stop` (model completed its task).

The PR was created successfully (confirmed in session log: `https://github.com/Majowka/mesh-manager/pull/3964`). However, the worker did not post a `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` comment. This is a defensive guard — `ready_missing_summary` exists to prevent false completions where a pre-existing PR is incorrectly credited to the current worker. In this case, the guard mis-fires because the worker genuinely created the PR but skipped the MERGE_SUMMARY posting step.

Two-part fix needed:

1. **Worker side** (defensive): After `gh pr create`, always post a MERGE_SUMMARY comment. Workers using raw `gh pr create` outside of full-loop helpers should include a MERGE_SUMMARY step.

2. **Runtime side** (resilience): The `ready_missing_summary` case should still transition the issue to `status:in-review` before "retaining claim", so the stale scan doesn't produce a re-dispatch risk. Currently it leaves the issue in an active lifecycle state (`status:in-progress`) that the stale scan aggressively resets.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually add `status:in-review` label to issue #3896 and remove `status:available` to prevent re-dispatch on top of approved PR #3964

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.273
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21
- Worker session: `issue-3896` / `ses_fee0334f4ffeVitjfsyGv8Cs2D` / PID 2195347
- Worker log: `/run/user/1000/aidevops/pulse/pulse-Majowka-mesh-manager-3896.log` (line 276)
- Affected files: `headless-runtime-worker.sh:1902-1907`, `pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:45-52`

## Additional Context

The `ready_missing_summary` classification is designed to protect against a PR created by a different actor being incorrectly claimed as the worker's completion. The design intent is sound. The gap is that when the classification fires (correctly or not), no `status:in-review` transition is made — so a stale scan, which correctly detects "no live process, but issue in active state", resets the issue to available.

The fix-worker created by the re-dispatch would create a NEW PR on top of an existing APPROVED PR — potentially creating a merge conflict, duplicate CI runs, and reviewer confusion.

See-also: marcusquinn/aidevops#30394 (related — both bugs prevent automated PR lifecycle completion for worker-created PRs)
