title: Async codegraph init in dispatcher-created worktrees so headless workers get symbol navigation instead of grep fallback
body:
## Description

Dispatcher-created linked worktrees never contain a usable CodeGraph index, so every headless worker falls back to plain grep/read for code navigation.

`.codegraph/` in a fresh worktree holds only the committed `.gitignore` placeholder — the SQLite DB, WAL files, and daemon socket are machine-local and gitignored by design. Meanwhile the canonical checkout has a live index. When a worker calls `codegraph_explore`, the tool reports the project as not indexed and its own guidance instructs the agent to stop using it and fall back to built-in search for the rest of the session.

Observed 2026-08-24:

- Worktrees under `<worktrees-base>/<repo>-feature-auto-*/.codegraph/` contain only `.gitignore`
- Canonical checkout `<canonical-checkout>/.codegraph/` has a live `codegraph.db` (~116 MB) plus an active daemon
- `rg codegraph` across the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` returns zero matches — no dispatch or worktree-helper integration exists
- A worker session paused on a maintainer permission request (`external_directory` via `grep`) while investigating config that in-worktree symbol navigation should have covered

## Expected Behavior

After `git worktree add`, the dispatcher starts an asynchronous, bounded, best-effort `codegraph init <worktree>` in the newly created worktree. Long-lived workers gain symbol-level navigation mid-session; short workers keep the grep fallback with no behavior change. Init failure must never block or fail the dispatch.

No sandbox changes are required: the index lives entirely inside the worker's own worktree, so no `external_directory` permission is involved. This matches the existing framework pattern of avoiding generic external-directory approvals (see `headless-runtime-launch.sh` attachment design).

Measured cost for a mid-size webapp repo (2661 tracked files): `codegraph init` completes end-to-end in **51.8 s wall clock** (14.3 s graph build: 1,653 files, 29,640 nodes, 78,710 edges) and produces a **~100 MB** `.codegraph` DB. Because init runs asynchronously alongside worker startup, added dispatch latency is zero — the index becomes usable ~50 s into the worker session. Short-lived batches that finish sooner simply keep the grep fallback, so gating init by expected session duration/tier is a cheap optional refinement. CodeGraph also indexes YAML (145 files) and Go (84 files) in this repo, covering bridge config surfaces workers currently probe via grep.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (fresh dispatcher-created worktree):

```
ls -a <worktree>/.codegraph
```

**Actual output**:

```
.gitignore
```

**Comparison** (canonical checkout, same repo):

```
ls -la <canonical-checkout>/.codegraph
→ codegraph.db (~116 MB), codegraph.db-shm, codegraph.db-wal,
  daemon.log, daemon.pid, daemon.sock
```

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation (enhancement proposal — the gap observations above are direct command outputs from this session; no owning-path trace was captured because the integration simply does not exist yet)

**Owning-path proof**: `rg codegraph` over the deployed framework scripts directory returns zero matches; worktree creation lives in the dispatcher/worktree-helper path, which has no CodeGraph hook.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Let pulse/dispatcher create a linked worktree
2. `ls -a <worktree>/.codegraph` → only `.gitignore`
3. Compare with the canonical checkout, which has a full live index

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.289 (latest)
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, bash 5.2.21
- Working repo: <private webapp repo> (develop)
- gh CLI: 2.89.0
- CodeGraph: npm `@colbymchenry/codegraph` 1.5.0

## Additional Context

- Alternative considered and rejected: pointing workers at the canonical checkout's shared index. It would require a new scoped permission class (blanket `external_directory: allow` is already flagged as a violation by `audit-agent-deployment.sh`), and index answers would describe base-branch content rather than the worker's branch — misleading line numbers and missing new symbols.
- Possible upstream follow-up: codegraph currently resolves strictly per-directory ("nearest `.codegraph/` at or above the path"). A per-commit/OID-aware shared index for git worktrees of one repo could be proposed upstream if this enhancement lands well.

title: Fix PR merge hygiene checkout for non-main base branches
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Make PR-merge issue hygiene resolve `TODO.md` from the merged pull request's trusted base branch instead of hardcoding `main`. A merged PR targeting `develop` or another maintained base branch must find its existing linked-issue mapping and complete issue/TODO hygiene without weakening fork safety.

## Why

A managed downstream repository uses `develop` as its active PR base while `main` is release-only. A merged task PR had an exact `TODO.md` mapping on `develop`, but `Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` checked out `main` and failed closed because the linked issue had no mapping in that snapshot. The linked issue therefore retained stale lifecycle metadata until manually repaired. The resolver behaved correctly; it received the wrong branch snapshot.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The faulty checkout and regression-test surface are verified, but the worker must preserve `pull_request_target` trust boundaries while choosing the safest base-ref expression.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` — `sync-on-pr-merge`, especially `Checkout repo before closing-hygiene validation` around lines 901-907.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pr-merge-checkout-order.sh` — extend the existing workflow-structure regression coverage.

### Complete Write Surface

Do not change downstream caller workflows or relax `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh`. The reusable workflow owns the faulty `ref: main`; the resolver's exact-mapping failure is the required safety behavior when the selected snapshot genuinely lacks a mapping.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace the hardcoded caller checkout ref with the merged PR's trusted base branch/ref context.
2. Update the adjacent security comment so it describes trusted base-branch checkout rather than assuming every repository merges to `main`.
3. Preserve the existing checkout order, early shim staging, framework restoration, Git-guard activation, and post-job cleanup invariants.
4. Extend `test-issue-sync-pr-merge-checkout-order.sh` to fail if closing-hygiene validation regresses to a literal `main` checkout and to require the trusted PR base ref.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Never check out fork head code in the `pull_request_target` path.
- Support repositories whose default/release branch differs from the PR base branch.
- Keep fail-closed exact `TODO.md` mapping semantics; do not turn a missing mapping into a warning or bypass.
- Do not replace the validated caller snapshot with a later checkout before proof-log mutation.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- Confirmed `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` hardcodes `ref: main` in the closing-hygiene caller checkout.
- Confirmed `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh` fails at `map_issue_tasks()` only because the checked-out `TODO.md` snapshot lacks the linked issue mapping.
- Confirmed `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pr-merge-checkout-order.sh` already owns checkout-order and trust-boundary assertions.

## Reproducer

1. Configure a managed caller repository so pull requests merge into `develop` while `main` remains release-only.
2. Add a `TODO.md` entry on `develop` containing an exact linked-issue mapping for an open task issue.
3. Merge the corresponding task PR into `develop` and let the reusable `Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` workflow run.
4. Observe that `Checkout repo before closing-hygiene validation` checks out `main`, after which `issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh` reports that the closing issue has no exact linked-issue mapping even though the mapping exists on the merged PR's base branch.

**Symptom command**:

```bash
bash __aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh TODO.md "10107" "t18311" ""
```

**Actual output**:

```text
ERROR: closing issue has no exact linked-issue mapping in TODO.md: #10107
```

**Expected output**: The resolver finds the exact mapping from the merged PR's trusted base-branch `TODO.md` snapshot and allows closing hygiene to continue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A merged PR targeting `develop` reads `TODO.md` from trusted `develop` state and resolves an exact linked-issue mapping.
- A merged PR targeting `main` continues to behave as before.
- Fork head code is never checked out by the write-capable merge-hygiene job.
- Missing or duplicate mappings still fail closed.
- Existing checkout-order and Git-shim safety tests remain green.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pr-merge-checkout-order.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pr-merge-checkout-order.sh
```

Also run the repository's workflow/YAML validation command that covers `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`.

title: Add audited deployment copies to non-Git runtime targets
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Add a narrow audited helper for synchronizing a verified Git worktree subtree into an intentionally non-Git deployment directory, such as a stable unpacked browser-extension folder.

## Why

The OpenCode pre-edit adapter correctly requires its target workdir to be a Git worktree. That protects repository edits, but it leaves no supported contract for the separate deployment step where reviewed files must be copied into a stable non-Git runtime directory.

Current investigation found:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/pre-edit-check-tool.mjs` intentionally rejects a non-Git destination.
- `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` has useful exact-SHA, clean-source, locking, staging, and destination-boundary patterns, but is intentionally restricted to the aidevops runtime deployment path.
- `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror` is for canonical Git mirror synchronization and must not be generalized for this use.
- No existing helper supports an arbitrary reviewed worktree subtree → explicitly authorized non-Git deployment target.

The workaround is manual backup plus `rsync --delete`, followed by a source/destination comparison. That can be made deterministic without weakening the repository pre-edit gate.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

The helper would own destructive destination synchronization, allowlisting, rollback, symlink handling, and source-provenance verification. Those safety boundaries need an explicit design before implementation.

## Proposed approach

1. Add a separate deployment-copy helper; do not add a bypass to the Git worktree pre-edit check.
2. Require:
   - a source inside a linked Git worktree;
   - an expected source commit SHA;
   - a clean source subtree or an explicit reviewed-tree proof;
   - an absolute destination that exactly matches an explicit allow/approval argument;
   - rejection of root, home, repository metadata, symlinked destinations, and ambiguous paths.
3. Stage the new tree transactionally, preserve a rollback copy, then converge the destination.
4. Verify source and destination content exactly after deployment.
5. Provide dry-run and machine-readable result modes.
6. Keep validation commands declarative or caller-owned; do not add arbitrary command execution to the helper.

## Files

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/deployment-copy-helper.sh` — proposed command surface; rename only if an existing deployment-helper boundary is a better fit.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-deployment-copy-helper.sh` — disposable worktree/destination fixtures and destructive-path rejection.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md` or the closest deployment safety reference — distinguish repository editing from non-Git artifact deployment.
- `REFERENCE: .agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` — reuse its exact-SHA, source cleanliness, lock, staging, and destination-fence patterns without broadening its fixed destination.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The helper refuses canonical checkouts, dirty/unverified source subtrees, source SHA mismatches, symlinked paths, and dangerous destinations.
- [ ] Destination deletion occurs only after exact explicit authorization and successful staging.
- [ ] A failed deployment leaves the previous destination recoverable and reports the rollback location without exposing private paths publicly.
- [ ] Successful deployment proves destination content exactly matches the approved source subtree.
- [ ] Dry-run performs no destination mutation and reports the planned add/change/delete set.
- [ ] The existing pre-edit worktree requirement remains unchanged and fail closed.
- [ ] Tests cover paths with spaces, interrupted staging, concurrent attempts, stale locks, destination-only files, rollback, and Bash 3.2 compatibility.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-deployment-copy-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/deployment-copy-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-deployment-copy-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

## Rollback

Remove the additive helper and documentation. No repository-edit guard or stored schema should require migration.

title: merge-stuck: pulse merge throughput collapse (5 consecutive zero-progress cycles)
body:
<!-- merge-stuck:zero-progress -->
## What

The pulse deterministic merge pass has had **5 consecutive cycles** with eligible-unmerged PRs but zero merges. The threshold is `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.

## Why

Eligible-unmerged means `APPROVED + MERGEABLE + !draft + !hold-for-review`. When this is non-zero AND the merge count is zero across multiple cycles, the merge pass is structurally blocked — gates failing closed (e.g. branch-protection 404 mis-fire), GraphQL exhaustion, repo-allowlist mismatch, or a regression in the merge gates themselves.

## How

### Files Scope

Investigation only — no `Files Scope` declared.

### Snapshot

```
eligible_unmerged_this_cycle=1, eligible_stuck_count=0, zero_progress_cycles=5
```

### Investigation steps

1. Read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` since the meta-issue was filed (`grep 'Merge pass: skipping' `) — the per-PR skip reason is logged for every cycle.
2. Cross-check `pulse-stats.json` for circuit-breaker fires and the `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips` counter — if non-zero, the t2922 fail-closed path is mis-firing.
3. Reproduce the merge gate decision for one stuck PR via `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` — it explains what the pulse decided and why.
4. Apply the fix (often a one-line gate adjustment) and verify the next cycle drops zero-progress to 0.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause of the throughput collapse identified.
- [ ] At least one of the stuck PRs successfully auto-merges.
- [ ] `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles` reads 0 in `pulse-stats.json`.

## Session Origin

Filed automatically by `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (t3193). The detector resets the zero-progress counter on any successful merge — if the meta-issue is stale (cause already resolved), close it manually.

<sub>Source: pulse-merge-stuck-detector. Threshold env: `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.</sub>

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
```

title: merge-stuck: pulse merge throughput collapse (5 consecutive zero-progress cycles)
body:
<!-- merge-stuck:zero-progress -->
## What

The pulse deterministic merge pass has had **5 consecutive cycles** with eligible-unmerged PRs but zero merges. The threshold is `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.

## Why

Eligible-unmerged means `APPROVED + MERGEABLE + !draft + !hold-for-review`. When this is non-zero AND the merge count is zero across multiple cycles, the merge pass is structurally blocked — gates failing closed (e.g. branch-protection 404 mis-fire), GraphQL exhaustion, repo-allowlist mismatch, or a regression in the merge gates themselves.

## How

### Files Scope

Investigation only — no `Files Scope` declared.

### Snapshot

```
eligible_unmerged_this_cycle=1, eligible_stuck_count=0, zero_progress_cycles=5
```

### Investigation steps

1. Read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` since the meta-issue was filed (`grep 'Merge pass: skipping' `) — the per-PR skip reason is logged for every cycle.
2. Cross-check `pulse-stats.json` for circuit-breaker fires and the `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips` counter — if non-zero, the t2922 fail-closed path is mis-firing.
3. Reproduce the merge gate decision for one stuck PR via `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` — it explains what the pulse decided and why.
4. Apply the fix (often a one-line gate adjustment) and verify the next cycle drops zero-progress to 0.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause of the throughput collapse identified.
- [ ] At least one of the stuck PRs successfully auto-merges.
- [ ] `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles` reads 0 in `pulse-stats.json`.

## Session Origin

Filed automatically by `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (t3193). The detector resets the zero-progress counter on any successful merge — if the meta-issue is stale (cause already resolved), close it manually.

title: Headless worker silent deaths are undiagnosable: no per-attempt correlation ids, timestamps, or last-stage traces in shared log
body:
## Observed

Headless review-thread response workers in a private mesh-admin repo die silently between `post_worker_prepare` and runtime invocation (`worker_runtime_not_invoked`, exit=1) or right after opencode boot with zero model sessions (`worker_noop_zero_output`, exit=0). Bursts of 2-5 workers die within the same second. Root cause cannot be determined from logs because:

1. All concurrent workers append to ONE shared logfile with no per-attempt correlation id on `[lifecycle]` lines and no timestamps on `[INFO]`/`[exit-trap]` lines — attributing an interleaved `waiting_for_worker pid=X` or `exit-trap` line to a specific launch is guesswork.
2. `_execute_run_attempt` has early-return paths (`_prepare_run_attempt_command`, `_create_run_attempt_files`, `_configure_run_attempt_context`) that return non-zero without any persistent record beyond a stderr `print_error` that may interleave into the wrong attribution.
3. Exit-trap classification then guesses (`worker_runtime_not_invoked`) without recording which check failed or the last completed lifecycle stage.

Example timeline (single PR, one hour): 5 consecutive launches, each reaching `post_worker_prepare`, none producing ndjson output, outcomes alternating between `worker_noop_zero_output` and fake-success `clean`/`meaningful_remediation`.

## Impact

- Silent-death root cause is undiagnosable from production logs.
- Fake-success outcomes (`clean` + `meaningful_remediation` for zero-work runs) trigger the full 3600s fingerprint cooldown instead of the 90s infrastructure retry, multiplying time-to-recovery by ~40x.

## Requested fix

1. Add a unique `attempt_id` to every `[lifecycle]`, `[SANDBOX]`, and `[exit-trap]` line, plus ISO timestamps on ALL lifecycle lines (currently only scanner-side lines have them).
2. Persist a per-attempt state file (last completed lifecycle stage, pids, exit path) under the existing pr-review-thread-response state dir so a dead attempt leaves an attributable trace.
3. In the EXIT trap, record the last completed lifecycle stage explicitly when runtime-invocation flag is unset, instead of the generic `worker_runtime_not_invoked`.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh` (lifecycle emit points)
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` (`_execute_run_attempt`, observers)
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` (exit-trap classification)
- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` (state dir already exists — reuse)

## Verification

1. Kill a worker mid-launch (SIGKILL between lifecycle stages); confirm the state file identifies exact last stage and attempt_id.
2. Run two overlapping dispatches; confirm every log line is attributable to its attempt_id without ambiguity.
3. Existing tests pass: test-watchdog-stall-cap.sh, test-headless-runtime-worktree-tests.sh.

title: Exit classifier counts session existence, not model activity: zero-work runs recorded as clean/meaningful_remediation and trigger 3600s cooldown
body:
## Observed

Worker exits with status 0 are classified by `classify_worker_exit` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`, ~line 707) as:

- 0 opencode sessions created since start -> `worker_noop_zero_output` (retryable infrastructure, fast retry) — correct
- >=1 session -> `clean` — WRONG

An opencode session row is created at runtime boot, BEFORE the model produces any output. A worker whose model call fails instantly (provider error, auth, sandbox egress failure) still owns a session row, so it is classified `clean`.

Then `_hrff_retry_class_for_reason` (~line 1000) hits the default branch for unknown reason `clean`:

```bash
*) if [[ "$session_count" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
       printf '%s\n' "$_HRFF_RETRY_CLASS_REMEDIATION"   # meaningful_remediation
```

Result: a zero-work run is recorded as `reason=clean, retry_class=meaningful_remediation` — a fake success. The dispatch scanner treats it as completed remediation and applies the full fingerprint cooldown (default 3600s) instead of the 90s infrastructure retry.

## Evidence

Private mesh-admin repo, single PR, same hour: two workers each lived <90s, produced zero ndjson events, zero commits, zero thread replies, never invoked mark-complete/mark-blocked — both outcomes recorded `reason=clean / retry_class=meaningful_remediation`. Meanwhile the prompt contract states: "A successful process exit or prose report is not a terminal state."

## Requested fix

1. In `classify_worker_exit`, count MODEL ACTIVITY (message rows / tool-call parts in the isolated DB since start_epoch_ms), not session existence. Zero activity -> `worker_noop_zero_output`.
2. Remove `clean` from the unknown-reason fallback path: an exit-0 worker that never ran a terminal-state command (`mark-complete`/`mark-blocked`) must classify as failure/noop, not remediation.
3. Optionally: scanner-side effect verification — compare head SHA before/after plus thread reply count; zero delta -> treat as noop regardless of claimed class.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` (`classify_worker_exit`, `_hrff_retry_class_for_reason`)
- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` (outcome consumption, optional effect check)

## Verification

1. Synthetic run: boot opencode, fail first model call, exit 0 -> outcome must be `worker_noop_zero_output` / retryable_infrastructure.
2. Real remediation run (commits pushed + threads replied) still classifies `meaningful_remediation`.
3. shellcheck clean; existing tests test-headless-runtime-oauth-pool-gate.sh etc. pass.

title: Canary and small-model selection ignore oauth-pool cooldown: dead providers probed every dispatch cycle
body:
## Observed

`_select_canary_model` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`, ~line 1973) takes the first model from `get_configured_models()` without consulting oauth-pool cooldown state. `get_configured_models` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:54`) filters candidates only by allowlist and `provider_auth_available` (token existence) — never by quota/cooldown.

- opencode logs filled with `AI_APICallError: The usage limit has been reached` bursts exactly matching worker launch windows
- each wasted probe adds ~90s timeout churn per dispatch cycle

2. Clear cooldown; confirm provider re-enters candidates.

title: Custom model-routing-table.json silently ignored on schema mismatch: no warning when override is inert
body:
## Observed

`model_tier_candidates` (`.agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh`, ~line 135) validates each routing table with:

```
jq -e '((.tiers[$canonical].models // ...) | type) == "array"'
```

If the check fails for a requested tier, the table is silently skipped and the next table (or hardcoded fallback) applies. The user-customizable override `custom/configs/model-routing-table.json` — whose documented strategy is "Auto-failover between providers when credits exhausted" — can therefore be silently inert:

1. A tier without a `models` array (e.g. only a `reasoning` object) fails the check for that tier, and there is no warning.
2. Tier names in the custom file that do not match canonical tiers (`simple|standard|thinking`) are never requested, so those entries are dead weight with no signal.
3. Stale model IDs (previous generation names) pass schema validation but never match live provider catalogs.

## Evidence

Private deployment: custom table contained `simple`/`thinking` tiers with only `reasoning` objects plus outdated model IDs. Loader skipped it on every lookup; dispatches used the framework table's ordering instead. No log line, no warning, no metric indicated the override was disabled. Operator believed failover ordering was active; it was not.

## Requested fix

1. When `custom/configs/model-routing-table.json` exists but fails per-tier schema validation, emit a loud one-line warning (once per process) naming the offending tiers and the reason.
2. Add a `aidevops doctor`-style check (or extend an existing config validator) that reports: custom table found / parsed / ignored + why.
3. Document the required minimal schema in the custom table template comment: every canonical tier needs a `models` array of `provider/model` strings; `reasoning` keys must reference full model IDs.

- Optional: existing config-validation entry point for the doctor check

title: Body-only human CHANGES_REQUESTED review parks worker PR forever: thread remediation converges on NO_MATCH and never falls through to t2093 fix-worker route
body:
## Observed

In a private mesh-admin repo, a trusted human reviewer submitted a substantive top-level review with `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` and ZERO inline review threads (body-only feedback). For ~16h the deterministic merge pass logged identical cycles:

```
review-thread remediation converged ... no matching unresolved thread remained after CHANGES_REQUESTED review gate
preserving PR ... CHANGES_REQUESTED remains blocking and required checks do not need CI repair
```

The t2093 fallback (`_route_pr_to_fix_worker` -> `_dispatch_pr_fix_worker`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh:2372`) never executed, because `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`, ~line 339-425) returns 1 on the converged outcome before reaching the route. The linked issue stayed `status:in-review` behind the open worker PR (dispatch dedup treats an open worker PR as an active claim), so nothing could ever pick the work up. 34 identical no-op cycles over 16h.

When the reviewer later re-submitted the same findings AS inline threads, the thread remediation path matched immediately and dispatched a response worker within 10 minutes — proving the gap is specifically the body-only-review shape.

## Impact

Any human review that requests changes via top-level review body only (no inline comments) parks the worker PR indefinitely. No auto-merge (correctly blocked), no fix-worker routing, no re-dispatch. Requires manual human intervention to unblock.

## Requested fix

In `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate`: when thread remediation converges (`_PULSE_MERGE_REMEDIATION_OUTCOME == "converged"`) AND reviewDecision remains CHANGES_REQUESTED from a human/trusted reviewer, fall through to `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` (t2093) instead of returning 1 — i.e. close the PR, append the extracted top-level review bodies to the linked issue as a Review Feedback section, restore `status:available`, and let the next cycle re-dispatch. Keep existing behavior when unresolved threads exist (thread remediation stays preferred).

Note: `_build_review_feedback_section` already handles top-level review bodies (reviews_json path), so evidence extraction needs no new machinery.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (`_handle_changes_requested_review_gate`, ~339-425; converged branch ~399-406)
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh:2372` (`_dispatch_pr_fix_worker`, t2093)

## Verification

1. Synthetic repo: worker PR + body-only CHANGES_REQUESTED review -> next merge pass closes PR, appends Review Feedback section to linked issue, issue returns to status:available, next cycle dispatches a worker.
2. Regression: PR with unresolved inline threads still goes through thread remediation first (no behavior change).
3. Regression: coderabbit-nits-ok dismissal path unchanged.

title: Zombie permission gate: dispatch blocked forever by needs-maintainer-permissions event history after label removed without grant
body:
## Observed

`_dispatch_permission_history_requires_grant` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1189`) blocks dispatch by scanning ISSUE EVENT HISTORY for any past `needs-maintainer-permissions` labeled event, then requiring a current signed grant (`approval-helper.sh verify-permissions`). The check ignores the label's current state.

Failure sequence observed in a private deployment (issues #51/#54 of an aidevops-routines repo):

1. Worker requests a permission; `needs-maintainer-permissions` applied (2026-08-05 / 2026-08-21). Legacy request format recorded NO scope details — permission, tool, and target were empty in the blocker record.
2. 2026-08-24 13:30 — automation removes the label without a signed grant.
3. Every subsequent dispatch cycle: history check sees the old labeled event -> `verify-permissions` returns NO_APPROVAL -> dispatch blocked with `permission_grant_unverified`.
4. The requirement is now unknowable (no recorded scope anywhere) and effectively permanent: nothing will ever produce a matching grant for a request whose contents were never persisted.

Result: infinite pre-launch failure bounce (~10 attempts/day per issue), pure noise plus wasted API budget.

## Requested fix

1. Gate on CURRENT label state, not event history: if the label is absent, no grant should be required.
2. If history-based verification is kept for tamper-resistance, then when the label was removed WITHOUT a verified grant, emit a loud warning and either (a) re-apply the label for human review or (b) reset the requirement with an audit-log entry — never loop silently forever.
3. Persist full request scope (permission, tool, patterns, risk) at request time so late approvals are possible; legacy empty-scope requests should fail loudly at request time instead of creating unapprovable blocks.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (`_dispatch_permission_history_requires_grant`, ~1189)
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-permissions.sh` (grant verification)
- `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh` (request persistence)

## Verification

1. Reproduce: apply then remove `needs-maintainer-permissions` on a test issue without a grant; confirm dispatch proceeds (or surfaces a single loud warning + audit entry), not an endless block.
2. With label present and a signed grant: dispatch proceeds as today.
3. With label present and no grant: blocked as today.
4. shellcheck clean; related dispatch tests pass.

title: t18307: Preflight all external PR approval authorities before prompting
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `external fork PR approval preflight linked issue cryptographic authority` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 8 recent commits / 0 merged related PRs / 0 open related PRs reported for the target files
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — existing authority boundary remains unchanged, but aggregation spans review guidance and merge gates
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the defect needs a worker-owned regression fix, not an unverified seed

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-08-25
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive review/full-loop session
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** None
- **Blocked by:** None
- **Conversation context:** A maintained-repository review required three separate privileged approval interactions because PR metadata repair, final PR snapshot authority, and linked-issue authority were discovered sequentially. The user identified this as a major process failure.

## What

Add a non-mutating external-PR approval preflight that discovers every cryptographic authority dependency before asking the user to run `sudo aidevops approve`. It must report all missing issue and PR targets together and provide one mixed batch command after approval-bound metadata is final.

## Why

During PR #30677, the review first requested PR approval, then changed approval-bound linkage metadata, requested PR approval again, and only at merge discovered that linked issue #29938 also required authority. `pre-merge-gate` passed before the final merge authority guard rejected the operation. This wastes scarce human attention and trains users to distrust supposedly final approval prompts.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (exact command used):

```bash
./.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 30677 marcusquinn/aidevops

```

**Actual output** (observed behavior): The gate accepted review/readiness evidence before issue #29938 had cryptographic development authority. The subsequent merge path then stopped with:

```text
Merge blocked: external/fork PR linked issue #29938 lacks current cryptographic development authority

```

Before reaching that failure, approval-bound PR linkage metadata had also been repaired after the first PR approval, invalidating that snapshot and requiring another approval. The complete interaction required three privileged prompts rather than one precomputed batch.

**Expected output** (required behavior): Before the first approval prompt, a read-only preflight should identify required metadata repairs and every missing issue/PR authority target, then emit one mixed batch command only after the final PR snapshot exists.

**Causal status:** confirmed

**Owning-path proof:**

- **Production entry point:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:335` dispatches `pre-merge-gate`; `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh:337-387` validates readiness/review-bot state but does not evaluate external authority.
- **Call chain:** `cmd_merge` calls `cmd_pre_merge_gate` at `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:1942-1946`, then each merge transport calls `_merge_revalidate_transport_authority`, which invokes `_merge_guard_admin_merge_maintainer_review` at lines 933-940; linked-issue authority rejects at lines 433-456.
- **Integrated verification:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh:343-384` exercises external/fork authority enforcement, while the production `pre-merge-gate` path has no equivalent aggregate check. The live sequence above exercised both production commands.

**Call-site sweep:**

```bash
rg "cmd_pre_merge_gate|_merge_guard_admin_merge_maintainer_review|_merge_linked_issue_authority_clear" .agents/scripts/

```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The trust boundary is already decided by the final merge guard. The implementation must reuse that policy without weakening it, aggregate all missing targets, and coordinate helper output with review guidance.

## PR Conventions

Use a leaf PR with the normal closing keyword for this issue.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Issue-only avoids anchoring implementation before the helper interface is selected.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Current target files and recent collision results were inspected at HEAD.
- **Verification run:** Current behavior reproduced operationally; implementation checks are pending.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Recheck recent authority-gate changes before editing shared merge code.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` — make the pre-merge/pre-approval path invoke the same external-authority policy used by merge, while supporting an aggregate diagnostic mode.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` — refactor the final authority guard so diagnostics can collect every missing linked-issue and PR authority target without changing fail-closed merge enforcement.
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/review.md` — require linkage and other approval-bound metadata repair before the first prompt, then emit one grouped mixed issue/PR approval command.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` — add regression coverage for aggregate missing-authority reporting and unchanged merge denial.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` dispatches `pre-merge-gate`; `cmd_merge` calls that gate and then `_merge_guard_admin_merge_maintainer_review` before the GitHub merge write.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** The new preflight is read-only. Actual approval writes remain exclusively in `aidevops approve`; merge writes remain behind `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` and the existing final guard.
- **Tests/fixtures:** Extend the existing mocked external/fork authority cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no persisted schema/config is modified; if helper output becomes machine-readable, keep new fields additive in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Edit repository `.agents/` sources only; `setup.sh` owns deployment to user installations.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because existing `aidevops approve` records remain valid under their current snapshot rules and no data shape changes.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Reverting `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, and `.agents/workflows/review.md` restores prior sequencing without altering approval records.

### Reference Pattern

Use `_merge_guard_admin_merge_maintainer_review` and `_merge_linked_issue_authority_clear` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` as the canonical policy source. Do not duplicate or relax its checks. Follow the grouped approval-command pattern already documented in `.agents/workflows/review.md`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Separate authority evaluation from final enforcement so one read-only evaluation can return all missing issue targets plus the exact current PR snapshot target.
2. Expose that evaluation in `pre-merge-gate` or a dedicated pre-approval command and emit one deterministic mixed batch command.
3. Preserve the final merge-time authority check to defend against metadata or head drift after preflight.
4. Update review sequencing: finish closing linkage/body edits first, rerun preflight, then request approval once.
5. Add regression cases for one missing linked issue, multiple missing linked issues, missing PR snapshot authority, complete authority, and post-preflight drift.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** Diagnostic aggregation must never count as approval or bypass the final live guard.
- **Concurrency/atomicity:** PR head/body or linked issues can change after preflight; merge must revalidate live state and fail closed.
- **Migration/rollback:** No migration is needed; rollback removes only the new diagnostic path and preserves existing approval records.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Keep existing commands and human-readable success behavior compatible; additive output is preferred so older callers remain functional.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated preflights must return the same plan for unchanged state and omit already-approved targets.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** API uncertainty must produce no incomplete “final” approval command; fail closed and allow a safe retry after GitHub recovers.
- **Security:** Never infer issue authority from PR approval or vice versa.

### Verification Before Dispatch

**Surface mapping:** The focused authority test covers helper behavior, Bash/ShellCheck cover both modified shell files, and the repository linter covers the shared workflow and trust-boundary blast radius.

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh

```
Validates aggregate external/fork authority behavior and unchanged final denial.

```bash
bash -n .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh

```
Validates the modified shell surfaces.

```bash
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh

```
Required broad gate because shared merge/approval trust-boundary tooling is affected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For an external PR missing linked-issue and exact-head PR authority, one preflight reports every missing target and one copyable mixed `aidevops approve batch` command.
- [ ] Review guidance requires all approval-bound PR metadata changes before generating that command and requires regeneration after any metadata/head drift.
- [ ] A PR with all required authority passes the preflight without an approval prompt.
- [ ] Missing, stale, malformed, or API-uncertain authority still blocks the final merge; no existing trust check is weakened.
- [ ] Focused authority tests cover multiple missing targets and prove the final guard remains fail-closed.

title: t18308: Allow cleanup receipt adoption for merged fork PRs
body:

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `external fork PR cleanup receipt adoption exact head` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 8 recent commits / 0 merged related PRs / 0 open related PRs reported for the target files

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-08-25
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive review/full-loop session
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** None
- **Blocked by:** None
- **Conversation context:** PR #30677 merged successfully without a persisted cleanup receipt. Recovery could not adopt the exact-head linked worktree because the PR came from a fork.

## What

Allow `adopt-merged-receipt` to recover a missing cleanup receipt for a verified merged external/fork PR when the registered linked worktree exactly matches GitHub’s current head repository, branch, and head OID and the local target repository remains the maintained base repository.

## Why

The recovery command currently requires the PR head repository identity to equal the target repository. That can never be true for a genuine fork PR. In the observed case, adoption rejected an exact-head registered worktree, leaving `status --json` inactive with no cleanup receipt after a successful merge and no-release record.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (exact command used):

```bash
./.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh adopt-merged-receipt 30677 marcusquinn/aidevops

```

**Actual output** (observed behavior):

```text
[ERROR] Adoption blocked: merged PR head does not match this registered linked worktree and repository

```

Verified live metadata at reproduction time was: merged state, head OID `f28f149dcf988eb07009431756ad01d97ddb1b31`, head ref `bugfix/gh29938-fix-aidevops-issue-29938-release-receipt`, fork head repository `johncarterlives/aidevops`, and target repository `marcusquinn/aidevops`. The registered linked worktree was on that exact ref and OID. `status --json` returned inactive/none, and `finalize-receipt` separately rejected the missing cleanup receipt.

**Expected output** (required behavior): The command should distinguish the maintained target repository from the verified fork head repository, persist an exact-head `CLEANUP_DEFERRED` receipt, and remain idempotent.

**Causal status:** confirmed

**Owning-path proof:**

- **Production entry point:** `full-loop-helper.sh adopt-merged-receipt` dispatches to `cmd_adopt_merged_receipt`, which is the documented recovery command for an externally merged exact-head worktree.
- **Call chain:** `cmd_adopt_merged_receipt` calls `_merge_fresh_adopted_worktree_cleanup_target`; `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:1561-1568` requires `headRepository.nameWithOwner` to equal the target repository before returning a cleanup target, rejecting every genuine fork by construction.
- **Integrated verification:** The production command above reproduced the rejecting path. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh:435-459` covers idempotent adoption only after `configure_managed_repo_identity`, exposing the missing distinct-head-repository fixture.

**Call-site sweep:**

```bash
rg "adopt-merged-receipt|_merge_fresh_adopted_worktree_cleanup_target" .agents/scripts/

```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Existing merged-state, release-state, registered-worktree, branch, and exact-head constraints define the recovery boundary. Implementation must distinguish base-repository identity from verified fork-head identity without broadening either.

## PR Conventions

Use a leaf PR with the normal closing keyword for this issue.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Existing test fixtures can model the fork identity safely.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** The rejecting function and adoption tests were inspected at current HEAD.
- **Verification run:** The production-safe recovery command was rerun and reproduced the rejection.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Recheck receipt and worktree identity helpers if related cleanup code changes first.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` — repair `_merge_fresh_adopted_worktree_cleanup_target` so target/base repository and external head repository are verified as distinct identities.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh` — add a fork-head adoption fixture and preserve unsafe-evidence rejection cases.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `cmd_adopt_merged_receipt` consumes `_merge_fresh_adopted_worktree_cleanup_target`; `finalize-receipt`, `complete`, status reporting, and cleanup supervisors consume the persisted receipt.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** Only `cmd_adopt_merged_receipt` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` may create the missing receipt; existing receipts and conflicting terminal evidence must remain immutable/fail-closed.
- **Tests/fixtures:** Extend `test_cmd_adopt_merged_receipt_is_idempotent` coverage with distinct target and head repository identities.
- **Schemas/config:** Preserve the existing cleanup receipt schema and state values in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`; no config file changes are expected.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Edit repository `.agents/` sources only; `setup.sh` owns deployment.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no broad backfill or schema migration is needed; operators explicitly invoke adoption for a single already-merged PR with a missing receipt.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Reverting `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` restores the prior denial; valid receipts remain consumable without migration.

### Reference Pattern

Preserve the exact-head, branch, merged-state, no-release/published-release, linked-worktree registration, and idempotency checks already used by `_merge_fresh_adopted_worktree_cleanup_target` and `cmd_adopt_merged_receipt`. Model the successful managed-repository fixture in `test_cmd_adopt_merged_receipt_is_idempotent`, changing only the fork identity dimension.

### Implementation Steps

1. Fetch and validate both base repository identity and head repository identity from current GitHub PR metadata.
2. Require the current local repository/remote to resolve to the maintained target repository.
3. For a fork PR, require the registered worktree branch and exact local HEAD to match the verified GitHub head ref and OID while allowing the head repository to differ from the target.
4. Persist the same cleanup receipt fields and pending lease as the managed-repository path.
5. Keep idempotent replay and all unsafe-evidence rejection paths intact.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** Never accept same-content commits from an unrelated or ambiguous repository; bind the exception to live PR metadata and exact OID.
- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Re-fetch merged PR metadata immediately before receipt creation and reject drift.
- **Migration/rollback:** No migration is required; rollback restores the prior fork denial while retaining existing receipt compatibility.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Same-repository adoption behavior and receipt schema must remain unchanged so older cleanup supervisors can consume new receipts.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated adoption must produce byte-stable or semantically identical receipt evidence.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Missing API fields, unregistered worktrees, detached heads, branch mismatch, release uncertainty, API uncertainty, or existing conflicting receipts must fail without writing and allow safe retry after evidence recovers.

### Verification Before Dispatch

**Surface mapping:** The focused cleanup test covers adoption/receipt behavior, Bash/ShellCheck cover the modified helper, and the repository linter covers shared lifecycle infrastructure.

Validates the modified shell surface.

```bash
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh

```
Required broad gate because shared lifecycle cleanup infrastructure is affected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A merged fork PR with verified target repo, live fork head repo/ref/OID, and a matching registered linked worktree creates a durable `CLEANUP_DEFERRED` receipt.
- [ ] Repeating adoption is idempotent and does not rewrite valid terminal evidence.
- [ ] Same-repository adoption remains unchanged.
- [ ] Wrong repository, wrong branch, wrong OID, detached/canonical checkout, release uncertainty, API uncertainty, or conflicting receipt still writes nothing and returns failure.
- [ ] Focused tests model distinct base and head repositories and retain every existing unsafe-evidence regression.

title: bug(worktree-registry): recycled same-comm PID keeps stale owner row alive forever, blocking orphan worktree cleanup
body:
## Description

Stale ownership rows in `worktree-registry.db` block orphan-worktree cleanup forever when a registered owner PID is recycled by an unrelated process running the same binary name (comm). The reuse-detection helper compares only the process name, so a dead worker session's `bash` owner row is "confirmed alive" against any later unrelated `bash` process that inherited the PID. On busy hosts PIDs recycle within hours, so every silently-killed worker leaves a permanently undeletable worktree.

Observed impact chain (single host, 2026-08-25): silent worker deaths → stale owner rows → PID recycling defeats liveness check → `owned-skip` on every cleanup cycle → `_worktrees/` grew to 11 GB across 17 leaked mesh-manager worktrees → disk hit 90% (12 GiB free) → the dispatch disk-space gate blocked new dispatches (`pulse.log` 12:29Z: "disk space critical … available=5042024KB/4%").

## Expected Behavior

A registered owner whose process died — even if its PID was later reused by an unrelated same-name process — must be recognized as stale and unregistered after the existing dead-owner cooldown, so the guarded cleanup path can reclaim the worktree.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
grep 'registered owner alive' ~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log | tail -3
sqlite3 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worktree-registry.db \
  "SELECT worktree_path, owner_pid, owner_comm, COALESCE(owner_dead_seen_at,'') FROM worktree_owners WHERE worktree_path LIKE '%gh4046%';"
ps -o pid,comm,lstart -p 1421207
```

**Actual output**:

```
[pulse-wrapper] Orphan cleanup: skipping feature/auto-20260824-225709-gh4046 (...) — registered owner alive in registry
mesh-manager-feature-auto-20260824-225709-gh4046|1421207|bash|
    PID COMMAND STARTED
1421207 bash    Tue Aug 25 14:49:13 2026
```

The worktree was created 2026-08-24 22:57; the process now holding PID 1421207 started 2026-08-25 14:49 — an unrelated shell. `owner_dead_seen_at` is empty: the dead-owner cooldown at `shared-worktree-registry.sh:1131-1138` never engaged because `kill -0` succeeds against the recycled PID. Same pattern confirmed for gh4091 (pid 1664635 → bash started 14:57:41) and gh4097 (pid 1691212 → bash started 14:58:41).

**Expected output**: the row should have been marked dead-seen at first probe after worker death, quarantined for the cooldown, then unregistered automatically.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` (pulse-dispatch preflight, cadence gate ≥10 min) → `cleanup_worktrees` → `pulse-cleanup-worktree-state.sh:_worktree_owner_alive` (skip message at `:739`)
- **Call chain**: `_worktree_owner_alive` → `is_worktree_owned_by_others` (`shared-worktree-registry.sh:1173`) → `_wt_is_worktree_owned_by_others_for_resolved_pid` (`:1110`) → `kill -0 $owner_pid` succeeds on recycled PID (`:1131` skipped) → `_wt_owner_live_pid_reused_or_untrusted` (`:1150` → `:1059`)
- **Integrated verification**: production logs + registry DB + `ps lstart` captured live during the failure (above). The reuse-check function has exactly one call site (`:1150`). Existing test `tests/test-worktree-cleanup-proof-states.sh` covers other proof states but has no same-comm-recycle case — that test gap is part of this defect.

**Causal code** (`shared-worktree-registry.sh:1059-1075`):

```bash
_wt_owner_live_pid_reused_or_untrusted() {
	local wt_path="$1"
	local owner_pid="$2"
	local registered_comm
	local current_comm

	_wt_owner_created_at_expired "$wt_path" || return 1
	current_comm=$(_get_proc_comm "$owner_pid")
	registered_comm=$(_wt_owner_comm_for_path "$wt_path")
	if [[ -n "$registered_comm" && -n "$current_comm" && "$registered_comm" != "$current_comm" ]]; then
		return 0
	fi
	if [[ -z "$registered_comm" ]] && ! _is_ai_runtime_comm "$current_comm" && ! _is_shell_comm "$current_comm"; then
		return 0
	fi
	return 1
}
```

Two compounding defects:

1. `:1068-1070` — reuse is detected only when comms differ. A recycled PID running the same interpreter (`bash` == `bash`, the common case for headless workers) returns trusted.
2. `:1065` + `:1021` — the `WORKTREE_OWNER_STALE_LIVE_MAX_HOURS` TTL gate (default **168 h**) feeds into the same comm-only comparison, so even after expiry the same-comm recycle still returns trusted. The TTL cannot ever produce an unregister for same-comm rows; the guard defeats its own purpose.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a worktree owner (any dispatch does this) and kill the owning process hard (SIGKILL / process-group death — no EXIT trap runs).
2. Wait until the OS recycles the owner PID to any unrelated `bash` process (hours on a busy host).
3. Run the worktree cleanup cycle.
4. Observe `owned-skip — registered owner alive in registry` forever; the cooldown path never engages because `kill -0` succeeds.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manual `sqlite3` inspection of `worktree-registry.db` joined against `ps -o pid,comm,lstart` to identify stale rows (diagnostic).
- Planned manual deletion of stale owner rows so the next cleanup cycle can reclaim the leaked worktrees (remediation). Automating correct detection is this issue's fix.

## Siblings

- Recovery-bucket retention gap (trash grows unbounded, `candidate_count=0` always): filed as a sibling with `See-also:` cross-reference — the two together caused the observed disk exhaustion.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.290 (latest 3.32.290)
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, bash 5.2.21
- Working repo: mesh-manager (develop)
- gh CLI: 2.89.0

## Additional Context

Related closed issues, different mechanisms: #29402 (stale `owner_dead_seen_at` breaks launches — here the marker is never written at all), #28807 (systemd PID registered as owner — fixed), #28532 (cleanup lease mistaken for another owner under degraded cwd visibility). Suggested fix direction: persist the owner process start-time (e.g. `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 or `ps -o lstart` epoch) at registration and treat start-time mismatch as reuse in `_wt_owner_live_pid_reused_or_untrusted`; rows without a recorded start-time fall back to current logic plus the existing TTL. Consider also treating expired-TTL + shell/AI-comm rows as untrusted rather than trusted.

title: enhancement(worktree-recovery): automatic retention for recovery/worktrees — buckets accumulate forever under manual-review policy
body:
## Description

`~/.aidevops/recovery/worktrees/` (the trash backing guarded worktree removal) has no automatic retention. Every bucket is written with `storage-policy: manual-review`, `worktree-helper.sh recovery plan` always reports `candidate_count: 0`, and nothing ages buckets out. Combined with the archive treadmill (each dispatch creates a ~600 MB worktree; failed workers get archived by cleanup), the directory grew to **217 buckets / 31.6 GiB / 3,099,273 files** on a 116 GB host and contributed to disk exhaustion that tripped the dispatch disk-space gate (`pulse.log` 2026-08-25T12:29Z: "disk space critical … require at least 5242880KB and 5%").

The trash is on the same filesystem it protects: removal moves bytes from `_worktrees/` into `recovery/worktrees/`, so a full disk stays full. Observed treadmill evidence: producer PID 196036 archived eight ~540 MB buckets between 12:59–13:19Z on 2026-08-24; PID 125634 archived four ~640 MB buckets the next morning.

## Expected Behavior

Recovery buckets should have an automatic retention policy so the trash cannot grow unbounded, while preserving genuinely recoverable recent state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run dispatches normally for several days (including failing workers).
2. `du -sh ~/.aidevops/recovery/worktrees` — grows monotonically.
3. `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh recovery status` — all buckets `protected`.
4. `worktree-helper.sh recovery plan --output <path>` → `candidate_count: 0`, regardless of bucket age.

## Proposed Fix

Add a retention pass to the existing recovery-maintenance stage:

- Auto-prune buckets older than N days (default suggestion: 7) when the embedded manifest proves terminal upstream state: `.aidevops-worktree-recovery/{branch,created-at}` exist and the branch's PR is MERGED/CLOSED/GONE.
- Keep buckets that contain unmerged WIP (failed-worker archives with dirty diffs) longer, or surface them for explicit review instead of deleting.
- Report pruned counts/bytes in `storage-inventory-helper.sh` output so the trend is visible before disks fill.

The manifest data needed for safe automation already exists in every bucket (verified this session).

## Workarounds Applied

Manual two-pass deletion this session (2026-08-25): 102 buckets ≥48 h old (~5 GB) plus 115 buckets <48 h whose embedded PR was MERGED/CLOSED/GONE (~26 GB), each verified via `gh pr view` against the manifest branch. Disk went 90% (12 GiB free) → 65% (41 GiB free). This must be repeated manually forever without retention.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.290 (latest 3.32.290)
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, bash 5.2.21
- Working repo: mesh-manager (develop)
- gh CLI: 2.89.0

## Additional Context

Related: #29803 (compact archive + restore commands — added tooling, not retention), #30443 (recovery maintenance pressure-check fail-closed).

See-also: #30709 — the PID-reuse registry blind spot that prevents cleanup from removing leaked live worktrees in the first place (the other half of the observed disk exhaustion).

title: Fresh approval verification must precede repeat sudo requests
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Description

Interactive full-loop sessions can rely on an earlier `NO_APPROVAL` snapshot after a maintainer has just completed `sudo aidevops approve`. The session may then retry the privileged command, hit a non-TTY `sudo` failure, and incorrectly ask the maintainer to approve again.

The prompt already says to run `approval-helper.sh verify` before reporting missing approval (`.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:64`), and the full-loop linked-author gate performs a fresh check once execution reaches `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state.sh:1114-1134`. There is no deterministic pre-execution guard covering an assistant-issued `sudo aidevops approve ...` command before that start path runs, so stale conversational state can still create needless privileged prompts and user friction.

## Expected Behavior

Before an interactive runtime executes or recommends another approval command after approval may have changed, it must query the authoritative current state for every target. Already-verified targets must be removed from the retry path, and the session must continue the requested workflow without asking for another signature.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
sudo aidevops approve issue 30699 30700 30701 30702 30703 marcusquinn/aidevops
```

**Actual output**:

```text
sudo: a terminal is required to read the password; either use the -S option to read from standard input or configure an askpass helper
sudo: a password is required
```

The session then asked the maintainer to run the same approval command. The maintainer had already run it. A fresh authoritative check immediately afterward returned this for every target:

```text
APPROVAL_REASON: proven-locked-continuity
VERIFIED
```

GitHub also showed a cryptographically signed approval comment on each issue, `needs-maintainer-review` removed, and `auto-dispatch` present.

**Expected output:**

The assistant should first run the equivalent of:

```bash
approval-helper.sh verify issue 30699 marcusquinn/aidevops
```

for every batch target, recognize all targets as `VERIFIED`, skip the redundant `sudo` command, and continue full-loop execution.

**Causal status:** confirmed

**Owning-path proof:**

- **Production entry point:** the interactive `/full-loop` route in `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md:56-99` / `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:56-99` after a user reports that approval has completed.
- **Call chain:** user approval signal → model uses an earlier `NO_APPROVAL` result → Bash attempts `sudo aidevops approve` → non-TTY failure → model asks the maintainer to repeat approval. The deterministic linked-author gate is not reached before the redundant command.
- **Integrated verification:** this session reproduced the failed privileged retry, then ran `approval-helper.sh verify issue <N> marcusquinn/aidevops` for all five targets and received `VERIFIED` for each.

**Causal code/history:**

```text
b7d64ac499 .agents/workflows/full-loop.md:64 added the prompt-only freshness rule.
54c80daf82 .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state.sh:1114-1134 added the authoritative start-time verification.
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Obtain and cache `NO_APPROVAL` for one or more external-author issues.
2. Have the maintainer approve the same targets in a trusted terminal.
3. Tell the interactive session that approval is complete and request full-loop execution.
4. Let the session act from the cached result before invoking the linked-author gate.
5. Observe a redundant `sudo aidevops approve` attempt or another request for approval.
6. Run a fresh verifier call and observe `VERIFIED`.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually ran the authoritative verifier for every batch target after the maintainer questioned the repeated request.
- Inspected current signed approval comments and labels instead of trusting the earlier snapshot.
- Skipped another privileged retry after fresh verification succeeded.

## Environment

- aidevops: v3.32.290
- OpenCode: v1.18.23
- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- Shell: Bash 5.3.15
- GitHub CLI: 2.98.0

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `approval not lasting fresh verification` → no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: recent approval continuity commits inspected; they preserve signed approval validity but do not enforce a fresh pre-command check.
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:64` and `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state.sh:1114-1134` match the claim.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — bounded enforcement inside an already-decided approval boundary; no weakening or new authority semantics.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the implementation should choose the smallest cross-runtime command-policy integration after focused inspection.

## What

Add a deterministic, current-state approval freshness preflight for assistant-issued approval commands. It must parse issue/PR batch targets, verify each target immediately before the privileged command path, suppress already-verified retries, and return actionable status for only genuinely unapproved or indeterminate targets.

## Why

Repeated root-password prompts and repeated approval requests waste maintainer attention, create doubt about whether cryptographic approval persists, and stall otherwise-authorized full-loop work. This is exactly the kind of deterministic state check that should not depend on model memory.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** the authority boundary and verifier are already defined. The task is bounded command-policy integration with explicit fail-safe behavior and focused regression coverage.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state.sh:1087-1158` and `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:56-99` — preserve the existing authoritative check and understand the uncovered pre-start path.
- **Load only if:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs` and Claude command-policy adapter references — only if shared `command-policy-helper.py` cannot enforce both supported runtimes directly.
- **Why:** the fix should be deterministic and cross-runtime without expanding always-loaded prompt guidance.
- **Stop when:** the approval command parser, verifier contract, mixed-batch behavior, and focused tests are identified.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/command-policy-helper.py` and its focused modules — recognize assistant-issued `sudo aidevops approve issue|pr|batch ...` commands and invoke a read-only freshness preflight before privilege escalation.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` — add or expose a batch-safe read-only verification entry point only if existing single-target `verify` cannot be reused cleanly.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh` — cover all-verified, all-unapproved, mixed, malformed, and indeterminate batches.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-verify-state.sh` — cover any new batch verifier contract.
- `EDIT only if needed: .agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` — record this prompt-only rule as hooked/partial once deterministic enforcement exists.
- `EDIT only if shared command policy is insufficient: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs` and its tests — preserve OpenCode behavior while maintaining Claude Code parity through the shared policy helper.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** OpenCode `tool.execute.before` invokes the shared command-policy helper through `quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs`; Claude Code command guards also route shell commands through `command-policy-helper.py`; full-loop start independently reads `approval-helper.sh verify` results.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because the freshness preflight is read-only; only the existing authorized mutation path in `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` may change GitHub state.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-verify-state.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-external-issue-author-gate.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/configs/command-policy.json` only if a declarative matcher is appropriate; otherwise preserve its current schema.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys scripts/plugins; no generated command documentation should be expanded.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` approval records remain valid and unchanged.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because reverting the focused command-policy matcher restores prior behavior without changing any signed approvals.

### Implementation Steps

1. Parse supported repository-qualified approval command shapes without evaluating shell content or accepting injected arguments.
2. Before privilege escalation, run a fresh read-only verification for each exact target against the explicit repository.
3. If every target is `VERIFIED`, block the redundant privileged command with a success-oriented message instructing the runtime to continue the requested workflow.
4. For a mixed batch, report the exact verified and still-unapproved subsets and provide the reduced approval command for only the latter; never discard indeterminate targets silently.
5. For `NO_APPROVAL`, allow the original command. For verifier/API/key indeterminacy, preserve fail-safe approval behavior while forbidding the runtime from claiming that approval is missing without evidence.
6. Keep `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:64` as a short invariant/pointer; do not add another long prompt rule.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** approval may land between targets in a batch; each result must come from the same immediate pre-command pass, and a retry must requery rather than reuse it.
- **Migration/rollback:** no state migration; rollback removes only pre-execution enforcement.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** old runtimes continue to rely on the prompt/start gate; new runtimes must accept existing `approval-helper.sh verify` output, including `APPROVAL_REASON` lines followed by `VERIFIED`.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated preflight is read-only and safe; already-verified approvals must remain valid.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** API or verifier failure must not be misreported as `NO_APPROVAL`, must not weaken the approval gate, and must not silently drop a batch target.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target functions:** determine during implementation; prefer a new focused parser/evaluator helper rather than expanding a command-policy function beyond the 100-line threshold.
- **Action required:** keep approval parsing and freshness evaluation isolated and independently testable.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-verify-state.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-external-issue-author-gate.sh
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** command-policy tests cover parsing and pre-exec disposition; approval tests cover authoritative output; full-loop tests preserve the existing gate; plugin tests prove OpenCode integration; changed lint covers shell/Python/JS quality.
- **Broad verification trigger:** only if shared command-policy behavior changes for commands other than `sudo aidevops approve`.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused parser/verifier tests pass.
- [ ] WIP commit created before any broad command-policy gate suite.
- [ ] Broader verification runs only if the shared command path changes beyond the targeted matcher.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** ensure a fresh approval check prevents repeated approval prompts and friction.
- **Preserved user directions:** never weaken cryptographic approval or infer authority from labels.
- **Trigger and evidence:** not triggered during filing.
- **Completed and verified:** issue evidence and current owning paths identified.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** implementation, focused tests, runtime integration, and review.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** relying on cached `NO_APPROVAL` or retrying `sudo` before verification.
- **Next safe route:** shared read-only command preflight.
- **Resume condition:** worker claims this issue.
- **Owner and status:** auto-dispatch worker; pending implementation.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/command-policy-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_*.py`
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-verify-state.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-external-issue-author-gate.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`
- `.agents/configs/command-policy.json`
- `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An assistant-issued approval command performs a fresh authoritative check for every exact target before privilege escalation.
- [ ] An all-verified batch performs no redundant `sudo` attempt and returns guidance to continue the requested workflow.
- [ ] A mixed batch identifies verified, genuinely unapproved, and indeterminate targets without dropping or weakening any target.
- [ ] A stale earlier `NO_APPROVAL` result cannot override a newly signed approval in the pre-command decision.
- [ ] API/verifier failure is never presented as proof that approval is missing.
- [ ] Existing approval signatures, full-loop author gates, and non-approval command-policy behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests and changed-file lint pass.

## Context & Decisions

- The approval gate itself worked correctly and all five signatures persisted; this issue addresses stale decision-making before the authoritative check.
- Do not weaken `needs-maintainer-review`, signed approval, issue locking, or snapshot continuity.
- Prefer deterministic enforcement over another always-loaded prompt instruction.
- No release/publication is part of this task.
