title: fix: recovery plan can exceed deadline without writing partial output
body:
## Summary

`worktree-helper.sh recovery plan` can exceed its declared `--deadline-seconds` by more than a minute and exit only when the caller kills it, without writing even a partial plan. This defeats bounded recovery classification and leaves disk cleanup unable to progress safely.

## Reproducer

On aidevops v3.32.296 with 260 recovery entries:

```bash
.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh recovery plan \
  --output ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/recovery-cleanup-plan-offset15.json \
  --offset 15 --max-classify 15 --deadline-seconds 180
```

Observed: the caller timed out after 240 seconds; the requested output file did not exist afterward, and no recovery-plan process remained. A prior 120-second run classified only 15/260 entries, so bounded continuation is required.

Expected: terminate within the requested deadline plus small fixed cleanup overhead and atomically publish a partial read-only plan containing `classification_deadline_exhausted=true` and `next_classification_offset`.

## Likely files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh` — classification deadline and child size-probe lifecycle
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh` — `recovery plan` argument handling/output publication
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh` — bounded deadline regression coverage

## Acceptance criteria

1. Deadline applies to blocking child probes as well as the outer loop.
2. A timed-out batch writes a valid partial plan atomically.
3. No child process survives return.
4. Runtime is bounded to deadline plus at most 30 seconds of finalisation overhead.
5. Existing recovery lifecycle tests pass, with a regression test using an intentionally slow classifier/size probe.

## Verification

Run `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh` and repeat the reproduction against a recovery root containing at least 15 entries.

title: fix: 31-minute Pulse service timeout kills workers during prelaunch
body:
## Summary

The systemd Pulse service has `TimeoutStartSec=1860`, but normal Pulse cycles now exceed 31 minutes. systemd terminates the entire control group during worker prelaunch, after claims and worktrees are created but before `headless-runtime-helper` starts. The next timer cycle repeats the work; no worker makes progress.

## Reproducer

Observed on aidevops v3.32.296 / OpenCode v1.18.25:

1. `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service` started PID 3846788 at `2026-08-31T09:51:47Z`.
2. The cycle spent 1130s in `preflight_early_dispatch`, with deterministic merge passes around 555s.
3. At 10:20-10:21Z it won claims for mesh-manager issues #4508, #4509 and #4510 and created linked worktrees for #4508/#4509.
4. Before any worker launch event, systemd reached the 1860-second start timeout and terminated the control group.
5. A replacement cycle started as PID 186891 at `2026-08-31T10:22:37Z`.
6. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue 4508 --json` reports the claim/worktree but `attempt_count=0`, no blocker, and no linked PR; no `headless-runtime-helper` worker process exists.

Unit evidence:

```ini
[Service]
Type=oneshot
KillMode=control-group
TimeoutStartSec=1860
```

## Impact

Dispatch can livelock indefinitely when merge/enrichment work consumes most of the service budget. Claims and large worktrees are repeatedly created, disk use grows, and clean auto-dispatch issues remain unimplemented.

## Likely files

- systemd/routine unit generation for `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` cycle budget/checkpoint handling
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` / dispatch launch path
- Pulse systemd and dispatch lifecycle tests

## Acceptance criteria

1. A normal cycle cannot be killed by the generated service timeout while a worker is between claim and durable launch/rollback.
2. Pulse computes remaining service budget before starting a dispatch candidate and checkpoints safely when insufficient.
3. Claims/worktrees created before interruption are deterministically resumed or rolled back on the next cycle.
4. Generated timeout is consistent with the maximum configured cycle budget, or long work is split into bounded services.
5. Regression test simulates systemd termination at prelaunch and proves the next cycle converges without duplicate worktree growth or zero-attempt livelock.

## Verification

Run Pulse with merge/enrichment stages delayed beyond 30 minutes, then verify one clean candidate reaches a durable worker launch and the service exits normally without `Terminated` in `pulse-wrapper.log`.

title: fix(storage): recovery maintenance can leak tens of GiB and never enter pressure mode
body:
## Problem

Automatic worktree recovery maintenance can grow the recovery store far beyond its 5 GiB soft limit while reporting `pressure_active=false` and reclaiming zero bytes. On a Linux runner, 264 recovery buckets occupied about 48 GiB and the filesystem reached 74% usage.

## Reproducer

1. Let asynchronous cleanup archive many frontend worktrees containing ignored `node_modules` directories into the default Linux recovery root.
2. Grow the root until a complete `du -sk` exceeds `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_RECOVERY_AGGREGATE_SIZE_TIMEOUT_TENTHS` (default 20 tenths).
3. Run `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh` or wait for `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`.
4. Observe maintenance JSON with `outcome:no-candidates`, `reclaimed_bytes:0`, `pressure_active:false`, `pressure_reason:aggregate-size-unavailable`, and `store_bytes:null`, although the root exceeds 5 GiB.
5. Observe individual archives around 600-730 MiB and classification counts dominated by `active_session_claim`, `archive_worktree_dirty`, and `sizing_unavailable`. A direct pass over 264 buckets can exceed five minutes.

## Root-cause evidence

- `worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh::_worktree_recovery_maintenance_pressure_json` leaves pressure inactive when aggregate sizing times out, so the 5 GiB threshold cannot trigger.
- `audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh::_worktree_copy_directory_once` uses full `cp -a`, including ignored/regenerable dependencies.
- `worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh::_worktree_recovery_plan_git_state` uses `--ignored=matching`, so copied ignored dependencies can classify an otherwise clean archive as dirty.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`
- Existing focused tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle.md` if policy semantics change

## Required change

1. Make aggregate-size unavailability enter bounded pressure handling instead of silently disabling the store-size limit; do not require an unbounded full `du`.
2. Prevent explicitly safe regenerable dependency/build caches from dominating archives while preserving tracked, staged, untracked, and ignored user work.
3. Ensure regenerable ignored content alone does not protect a terminal archive forever.
4. Preserve exact terminal-evidence classification, transactional apply, journal, receipt, canonical, and symlink guards.
5. Bound maintenance so it cannot consume an entire Pulse/systemd cycle.

## Acceptance criteria

- A store over 5 GiB whose aggregate sizing times out enters deterministic bounded pressure mode or an equivalent conservative fallback.
- A terminal clean archive containing only recognised regenerable caches can become a candidate; real user changes remain protected.
- Hundreds of buckets complete a bounded pass within the configured runtime budget and advance the cursor.
- Diagnostics separate aggregate sizing timeout, protected evidence, and retention policy.
- Existing apply safety invariants remain intact.

## Verification

- Extend and run `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh`.
- Extend and run `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`.
- Run ShellCheck/lint on modified shell files.
- Add a fixture containing a large ignored dependency cache and a real ignored user artifact, proving only explicitly safe regenerable content is excluded or discounted.

## Constraints

Do not fix this only by increasing timeouts, deleting the recovery root, weakening terminal evidence, or treating all ignored files as disposable.

title: fix(pulse-check): exclude non-runnable persistent quality-review issues from underfill queue
body:

In the live check, worker capacity was empty, but the only remaining scanner-eligible item was a persistent quality-review/audit issue. The Pulse state snapshot and dispatch candidate loop did not include that item as launchable implementation work, so the utilisation report produced a high-severity underfill finding that mixed dashboard/persistent work with worker-dispatchable issues.

title: fix(dispatch): classify zero-worker dedup_active_claim blocks during underfilled Pulse cycles
body:
## Summary

Pulse can report an issue as blocked by `dedup_active_claim` even when there is no active worker process. In the live underfill cycle, the dispatch loop skipped an available candidate as `dedup_active_claim`, then minimum-floor refill immediately skipped it again as `skip:already_assigned blocked:dedup_active_claim from current pulse cycle`. With `active_workers=0/2`, this creates a confusing no-progress state: capacity is free, but the candidate is excluded by claim/dedup state rather than being resumed, rolled back, or surfaced as a stale zero-worker claim.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**

```bash
.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report --json
.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 30m --json
```

**Actual output**

```json
{"active_workers":0,"available_slots":2,"dispatch_alive":true,"findings":[{"id":"pulse-underfilled-auto-dispatch-queue"}]}
```

Relevant Pulse log pattern from the same window:

```text
[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked issue=#8683 repo=awardsapp/awardsapp
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: #8683 blocked:dedup_active_claim benign dispatch block
[pulse-wrapper] Minimum worker floor refill: active=0/2, attempt=1/2 — re-enumerating candidates
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: skipping #8683 — skip:already_assigned blocked:dedup_active_claim from current pulse cycle
[pulse-wrapper] Minimum worker floor refill stopped: dispatch_max returned 0
```

**Expected output**

When no worker process exists, a candidate blocked by a claim should be classified into one of these deterministic states: active claim with live owner, stale claim pending takeover, zero-attempt infrastructure hold, or claim rollback/resume. It should not remain only a benign block while the worker pool is empty.

## Evidence

- `worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers` returned `0`.
- `pulse-check-helper.sh report` showed active workers `0 / 2` and emitted `pulse-underfilled-auto-dispatch-queue`.
- `pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 30m --json` showed no worker failures or stalls and no pre-launch blockers, but dispatch stage counts included repeated dedup stages.

title: Prevalidate runtime-risk evidence before commit-and-pr history mutation
body:
## Objective

Validate `commit-and-pr` runtime-risk evidence before staging, squashing, rebasing, or otherwise changing branch history.

## Observed evidence

During delivery in a managed private repository, the first `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` invocation supplied substantive live runtime evidence but did not include the literal `runtime-verified` marker. The helper first finalized three WIP commits into one commit and rebased, then blocked PR body generation with:

```text
Critical runtime risk requires runtime-verified evidence; PR body generation blocked.
```

A second invocation with the explicit marker succeeded. The safety gate was correct, but its ordering caused avoidable history mutation before detecting an invalid invocation contract.

## Root cause

Runtime-risk classification and `_resolve_runtime_testing_level` run after the commit/history-finalization phase. The arguments needed for this validation are already available before mutation.

## Reproducer

1. In a disposable linked worktree for a managed repository, create two or more WIP commits containing a change that the helper classifies as `Critical` runtime risk.
2. Record `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD`.
3. Invoke `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` with substantive testing text such as `live OpenCode smoke completed successfully`, but omit both `--testing-level runtime-verified` and the literal `runtime-verified` marker from `--testing`.
4. Observe that the helper prints `Finalizing WIP history into one commit` and performs its rebase before returning `Critical runtime risk requires runtime-verified evidence; PR body generation blocked.`
5. Re-run the two Git observations and confirm `HEAD` and the commit topology changed even though validation rejected the invocation before PR creation.

The expected behavior is rejection at step 3 before staging or history mutation.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — `commit-and-pr` phase ordering.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` — runtime-risk and testing-level validation.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` — focused risk-gate coverage.
- Relevant `commit-and-pr` lifecycle tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-helper*.sh`.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` — document the machine-readable testing contract.

## Implementation guidance

1. Add a non-mutating preflight that resolves runtime risk and testing level from the supplied summary/testing arguments before staging, commit squashing, rebase, push, or PR-body generation.
2. Preserve the existing fail-closed requirement for `High` and `Critical` changes and the substantive-evidence check.
3. Reuse the validated result during later PR-body generation rather than applying divergent duplicate logic.
4. Ensure an invalid testing contract leaves `HEAD`, index, worktree, upstream refs, and remote state unchanged.
5. Make the preferred explicit form visible in usage/docs, for example `--testing-level runtime-verified`, while retaining compatible marker detection if currently supported.

## Acceptance criteria

- An invocation missing required runtime-verified evidence fails before any branch, index, worktree, or remote mutation.
- A valid runtime-verified invocation follows the current commit, rebase, push, and PR creation path.
- Runtime risk and testing-level resolution have one authoritative result per invocation.
- Existing self-assessed, standard-risk, partial-success, and WIP-finalization behavior remains covered.

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` with before/after `HEAD`, status, and remote-call assertions for rejected input.
- Run the focused full-loop runtime-risk and commit-and-PR tests.
- Run ShellCheck on modified shell files.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — the safety policy is decided, but phase reordering and lifecycle regression coverage require normal implementation judgment.

title: consolidated: classify zero-worker dedup_active_claim blocks during underfilled Pulse cycles
body:
_Supersedes #30934 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

# Consolidated: classify zero-worker `dedup_active_claim` blocks during underfilled Pulse cycles

## What

Make Pulse classify `dedup_active_claim` blocks with enough evidence to distinguish a live owner, stale owner, zero-attempt infrastructure hold, and current-cycle duplicate suppression. When every worker slot is free, a claim that never reached a durable worker launch must be recovered (rollback/resume) or emitted as a high-confidence actionable blocker; it must not remain a benign dispatch block.

## Why

Pulse observed `active_workers=0/2` with `dispatch_alive=true`, then skipped the same available candidate first as `dedup_active_claim` and again as current-cycle `already_assigned`. The minimum worker-floor refill consequently stopped at zero dispatches despite free capacity. Diagnostics reported `pulse-underfilled-auto-dispatch-queue` without worker failures, stalls, or pre-launch blockers, so operators could not tell whether the claim had a live owner, was stale, or represented an infrastructure failure. The change must preserve deduplication safety: a genuinely live active claim must never launch a duplicate worker.

## Reproducer

```bash
.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report --json
.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 30m --json
```

Actual capacity output:

```json
{"active_workers":0,"available_slots":2,"dispatch_alive":true,"findings":[{"id":"pulse-underfilled-auto-dispatch-queue"}]}
```

Relevant log sequence from the same window:

```text
[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked issue=#8683 repo=awardsapp/awardsapp
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: #8683 blocked:dedup_active_claim benign dispatch block
[pulse-wrapper] Minimum worker floor refill: active=0/2, attempt=1/2 — re-enumerating candidates
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: skipping #8683 — skip:already_assigned blocked:dedup_active_claim from current pulse cycle
[pulse-wrapper] Minimum worker floor refill stopped: dispatch_max returned 0
```

Expected: with no worker process, the candidate is deterministically classified as a live-owner claim, stale-owner claim pending takeover, zero-attempt infrastructure hold, or claim rollback/resume. It must not remain only a benign block while the worker pool is empty.

## Evidence

- `worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers` returned `0`.
- `pulse-check-helper.sh report` showed active workers `0 / 2` and emitted `pulse-underfilled-auto-dispatch-queue`.
- `pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 30m --json` showed no worker failures or stalls and no pre-launch blockers, but dispatch-stage counts included repeated dedup stages.
- The candidate loop blocked a current issue on `dedup_active_claim` and then current-cycle already-assigned state without worker-launch evidence.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:1184-1234` — replace the broad `dedup_active_claim` normalization with evidence-rich classification for live owner, stale owner, zero-attempt claim, and current-cycle suppression.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:505-656` — use the classification in `dispatch_max()` and its candidate/floor loop handoff so a current-cycle, no-durable-launch claim is resumed or rolled back; otherwise log a non-benign actionable infrastructure block.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh:1-220` — expose the zero-worker claim state and its evidence in current-state diagnostics.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-check-report.jq:178-194` — ensure a zero-worker `dedup_active_claim` contributes actionable underfill evidence rather than a benign block.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh:149-198` — extend the existing no-worker stale-recovery fixture with active-claim evidence and a separate live-owner case.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh:355-420` — assert report classification for zero-worker and live-owner active-claim fixtures.

### Implementation Steps

1. Record claim provenance in the dedup decision: live worker/process evidence, durable launch evidence, attempt count, and whether suppression originated only in the active Pulse cycle.
2. Preserve the existing block for a live owner. For stale or zero-attempt current-cycle claims with no live worker and no durable launch, clear/requeue the transient assignment before floor refill, or emit a named non-benign infrastructure state when automatic recovery is unsafe.
3. Carry the named state through current-state and check-report output so an `active_workers=0` underfill cannot be reported as benign solely because `dedup_active_claim` was seen.
4. Keep this work focused on claim classification and recovery while Pulse is running; link the related zero-attempt livelock in #30930 but do not broaden the implementation to solve that issue.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Dedup safety:** live-owner evidence is a hard no-launch condition; recovery is limited to claims without live-worker or durable-launch evidence.
- **Idempotency/retry:** current-cycle rollback/resume must be safe if the floor refill repeats and must not create a second worker after a durable launch appears.
- **Diagnostics:** retain evidence rather than deleting claim records; surface the classified state and recovery decision in logs and JSON.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report --json
```

Expected: no-worker/stale claim fixtures emit a distinct actionable state and can recover or identify an infrastructure hold; live-owner fixtures remain safely blocked; no duplicate worker launch occurs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dedup_active_claim` records distinguish live owner, stale owner, zero-attempt claim, and current-cycle duplicate suppression using observable evidence.
- [ ] `pulse-check-helper.sh report` does not call a zero-worker `dedup_active_claim` benign when all worker slots are free.
- [ ] Minimum worker-floor refill recovers a current-cycle claim with no durable worker launch, or emits a high-confidence actionable blocker.
- [ ] Regression coverage separately proves no-worker active-claim diagnostics and live-worker active-claim safety.
- [ ] A genuinely live active claim never produces a duplicate worker launch.

## Context & Decisions

- The original reproducer recorded `worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers` as `0`, `pulse-check-helper.sh report` as `active_workers=0 / 2`, repeated dedup stages, and no worker failure/stall/pre-launch blocker; the specific failure sequence was `dedup_active_claim` followed by current-cycle `already_assigned` during minimum-floor refill.
- Per @marcusquinn: dispatch-path work is self-referential because workers execute through this code path; retain `tier:thinking` to avoid lower-tier attempts.

title: fix(update): surface stale local runtime when merged Pulse fixes are not deployed
body:
## Summary

Pulse/worker reliability fixes can merge upstream while the local deployed aidevops runtime continues executing stale scripts from an older canonical checkout or deployed bundle. After #30935/#30936/#30954 were merged, live diagnostics still showed old TODO protected-branch retry and dedup_active_claim benign-block behaviour because the local runtime had not picked up the merged commits.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**

```bash
git -C <aidevops-checkout> log --oneline -5
git -C <aidevops-checkout> log --oneline origin/main -5
diff -q <aidevops-checkout>/.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh <deployed-agents>/scripts/planning-publisher.sh
<deployed-agents>/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report --json
```

**Actual output**

```text
local HEAD: f83d59c81 Merge pull request #30921 ...
origin/main: newer commits including #30935 and #30936
deployed planning-publisher.sh matches stale local checkout
```

Live logs after the upstream merges still contained old symptoms:

```text
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main
[pulse-wrapper] TODO ref sync status=retryable_conflict ... reason=retryable_snapshot
[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim ...
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: ... blocked:dedup_active_claim benign dispatch block
```

**Expected output**

After upstream Pulse fixes merge, scheduled auto-update/deploy should either hot-deploy the fixed scripts or surface a clear stale-runtime blocker. Live diagnostics should not evaluate merged fixes against an old local bundle without saying the local runtime is stale.

## Evidence

- #30933 closed via merged PR #30935 with completion summary for protected-branch TODO publication deferral.
- #30932 closed via merged PR #30936 with completion summary for persistent-dashboard queue exclusion.
- #30942 closed via merged PR #30954 with completion summary for zero-worker active-claim classification.
- Local canonical checkout observed behind upstream default branch that already contained #30935/#30936.
- Deployed script content matched the stale local checkout.
- Pulse logs still showed GH006 retry patterns after #30935 had merged.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy.sh`
- READ: `.agents/reference/hot-deploy.md`
- READ: `.agents/reference/diagnostics-discipline.md`

## Implementation Notes

- Do not auto-reset dirty canonical checkouts. Preserve the dirty-worktree safety model.
- Add a diagnostic that compares the deployed script bundle, canonical checkout, and upstream default branch used by Pulse.
- If local deployment is stale because canonical checkout cannot fast-forward safely, report that as a first-class blocker with a safe operator action.
- Pulse health should include runtime staleness when it explains why recently merged fixes are not reflected in live behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `pulse-check-helper.sh report` or current-state diagnostics clearly reports when the running deployed script bundle is behind upstream fixes relevant to Pulse.
2. Auto-update/hot-deploy either updates the deployed bundle after safe upstream fast-forward or records a classified stale-runtime blocker.
3. A dirty canonical checkout is preserved and reported, not reset.
4. Tests cover stale canonical checkout, stale deployed bundle, and clean fast-forward deployment.
5. Operators can verify whether a merged Pulse fix is actually active locally without reading raw logs.

## Verification

Run:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report --json
```

Expected: stale-runtime fixtures emit a classified diagnostic; clean fixtures deploy or report current bundle.

title: fix(pulse): surface and enforce secondary GitHub cooldown despite GraphQL budget OK
body:
## Summary

Pulse wrapper can continue issuing repeated GitHub reads while the cooldown layer is already reporting `secondary-rate-limit active=true`. The live logs show clusters of HTTP 403 `API rate limit exceeded` responses immediately after repeated cooldown skip messages, while `pulse-check-helper.sh report` still renders GraphQL/API as OK. This makes operator diagnostics understate active REST/secondary API pressure and lets repeated timer invocations continue noisy GitHub calls.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**

```bash
<deployed-agents>/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh report
# then inspect the latest pulse wrapper log window for cooldown and HTTP 403 clusters
```

**Actual output**

```text
GraphQL/API: OK: remaining=5000/5000
[gh-cooldown] secondary-rate-limit active=true skip=read expires_at=<epoch>
gh: API rate limit exceeded ... (HTTP 403)
```

The same log window repeats the cooldown/HTTP 403 cluster across successive pulse invocations.

**Expected output**

When secondary cooldown is active, Pulse should suppress or sharply bound nonessential GitHub reads, and `pulse-check-helper.sh report` should surface active secondary cooldown separately from GraphQL remaining budget.

## Evidence

- Fresh monitoring showed `pulse-check-helper.sh report` with API budget rendered as OK and runner health HEALTHY.
- The same current log window showed repeated `secondary-rate-limit active=true skip=read` messages followed by multiple HTTP 403 `API rate limit exceeded` responses.
- Cycle health still showed dispatch candidates running but never successfully launching workers, with zero worker runtime events in the recent window.
- The observed failure mode is read-pressure/noise, not GitHub Actions saturation; merge-stuck diagnostics reported saturation false.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-check-report.jq`

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh`
- READ: `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md`
- READ: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

## Implementation Notes

- Do not treat GraphQL remaining budget as proof that REST/secondary limits are clear.
- Plumb the secondary cooldown state into pulse-check JSON and text output.
- Ensure helpers that see active cooldown fail closed before issuing more nonessential reads.
- Preserve essential safety reads, but bound retries and log a single classified suppression event per window.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Active secondary cooldown appears in `pulse-check-helper.sh report` even when GraphQL remaining budget is full.
2. Repeated timer invocations do not emit clusters of HTTP 403 reads while cooldown is active.
3. Deferrable Pulse stages are skipped or delayed under secondary cooldown with a classified reason.
4. Tests cover GraphQL OK + secondary cooldown active as a warning/finding state.
5. Existing GraphQL circuit-breaker behaviour remains unchanged for low GraphQL budget.

title: Add executable managed GitHub create subcommands
body:
## Description

Add executable `issue create` and `pr create` subcommands to `gh-write-helper.sh` so OpenCode agents can perform managed GitHub creation through the existing audited wrappers without dynamically sourcing shell libraries or creating one-off launcher scripts.

## Evidence

- `gh-write-helper.sh` currently accepts only `{issue|pr} edit`.
- `gh_create_issue` and `gh_create_pr` already implement body validation, signature handling, origin/status defaults, assignment policy, REST fallback, and cleanup, but they are exposed as sourced functions rather than executable commands.
- OpenCode command policy correctly blocks dynamic `source` launchers. During a Mainframe issue-publication task, this forced creation and ShellCheck validation of a temporary launcher before the managed create function could be called.
- #28790 / PR #28792 delivered streamed body support and executable safe **edits**. They did not add executable create actions. Exact issue and PR searches found no separate open or merged task for create subcommands.

## Pre-flight

- Memory recall: no prior reusable lesson for executable managed GitHub creation.
- Discovery: #28790 / PR #28792 is the only directly related merged work; no open related PR or duplicate issue was found.
- File references verified against the deployed current framework.
- Selected tier: `tier:standard` — the security boundary and wrapper behavior are established; this adapts the existing executable dispatcher without redesigning write policy.
- Seeded draft PR: skipped; the issue is implementation-ready and no code was written in the reporting session.

## What

The executable helper must support:

```text
gh-write-helper.sh issue create [managed create options]
gh-write-helper.sh pr create [managed create options]
gh-write-helper.sh issue edit <number-or-url> [managed edit options]
gh-write-helper.sh pr edit <number-or-url> [managed edit options]
```

Create actions must delegate to `gh_create_issue` and `gh_create_pr` with argument arrays unchanged. Existing edit behavior and exit codes must remain compatible.

## Reference pattern

Model the fixed resource/action dispatcher, cleanup traps, and safe-edit compatibility on the existing `gh-write-helper.sh`. Model streamed-body and wrapper-stub verification on `test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh` from PR #28792.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh:13-40` — extend usage and fixed action/resource dispatch to include managed create functions.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh` — add offline executable-create routing, body-file, stdin, rejection, and compatibility cases using the existing stubbed GitHub fixture.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md` — document the executable create path and retain same-command `--body-file` discipline.
- `EDIT IF REQUIRED: .agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` — only if the existing helper allowlist distinguishes actions; do not broaden arbitrary shell or raw GitHub writes.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** OpenCode Bash commands and framework helpers invoking `gh-write-helper.sh`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** existing `gh_create_issue`, `gh_create_pr`, `gh_issue_edit_safe`, and `gh_pr_edit_safe`; no new GitHub transport implementation.
- **Existing verification:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh`, command-policy tests, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint.
- **Schemas/config:** command-policy allowlist only if action-level matching requires it; preserve existing restrictions.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys scripts through the existing framework path; no separate generated copy should be added.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none; this is an additive executable interface.
- **Cleanup/rollback:** continue using the wrapper cleanup stack. Reverting the create dispatch leaves existing edit commands unchanged.

### Implementation Steps

1. Extend `usage()` to list both `create` and `edit` contracts.
2. Parse only the fixed resource/action matrix: `issue|pr` crossed with `create|edit`. Reject every other action with exit 2.
3. Dispatch create actions directly to `gh_create_issue "$@"` or `gh_create_pr "$@"`; do not duplicate validation, signatures, origin/status labels, assignment, retries, audit, fallback, or cleanup.
4. Preserve edit dispatch and number/URL argument behavior byte-for-byte.
5. Add offline tests proving path-backed and `--body-file -` create bodies reach the existing managed functions exactly once, while empty bodies and unsupported actions fail before a GitHub write.
6. Verify command policy still blocks arbitrary `source`, launchers, and raw managed-repository writes.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** existing unique body buffering and cleanup scopes remain authoritative; the dispatcher must not add shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** additive CLI actions only; old edit callers remain compatible.
- **Mixed-version compatibility:** callers on older deployments receive the existing usage/exit-2 response and must not fall back to raw writes.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the executable forwards one invocation; native-to-REST fallback remains owned by the managed create functions.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** preserve existing cleanup and durable-write reporting; do not mask a created issue/PR if a post-create optional action fails.
- **Security:** do not weaken command policy, permit arbitrary sourcing, bypass body validation, or expose body contents in diagnostics.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

Use stubbed GitHub commands for focused tests; no live issue or PR creation is required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh`
- `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gh-write-helper.sh issue create` delegates to `gh_create_issue` and supports normal path-backed and stdin body files.
- [ ] `gh-write-helper.sh pr create` delegates to `gh_create_pr` with the same body behavior.
- [ ] Existing issue/PR edit behavior and exit codes remain compatible.
- [ ] Unsupported resources/actions and empty or signature-only bodies fail before any GitHub write.
- [ ] Signature-once behavior, origin/status defaults, assignment policy, audit, cleanup, timeout, and REST fallback remain owned by existing wrappers and pass focused tests.
- [ ] Command policy continues to block arbitrary sourcing and raw managed-repository write bypasses.
- [ ] Focused tests, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint pass.

## Context and Decisions

- Extend the established executable helper instead of weakening OpenCode command policy.
- Reuse existing create functions instead of adding another GitHub transport or validation layer.
- Keep this change separate from issue-body format enhancements; only the executable creation gap is repeatedly evidenced and currently unresolved.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none.
- **Related completed work:** #28790 / PR #28792.
- **External:** none; verification is offline with existing stubs.

title: fix(storage): recovery maintenance deadline excludes full inventory traversal
body:
Problem: recovery maintenance advertises bounded scanning and a deadline, but performs an unbounded full-store inventory before either bound applies. On a real store with 293 archives, MAX_SCAN=1 and DEADLINE_SECONDS=15 exceeded an external 35-second timeout without entering the scan. Root cause: .agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh:227 calls worktree_recovery_inventory before the bounded scan; .agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:999-1030 traverses every recovery bucket; each record invokes full archive validation; .agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:853 runs git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all for every archive. Two representative validations took 0.45 s and 0.58 s, predicting roughly 132-170 seconds for 293 archives before bounded classification. The deadline test at .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh:1249-1308 stubs _worktree_recovery_maintenance_inventory_file, masking pre-scan cost. This reproduces after merged PR #30955 for #30931; deployed and repository helper hashes match. Required behaviour: limit expensive validation to the durable cursor/max_scan window; include pre-scan inventory and expensive subprocesses in the runtime bound; preserve archives and report continuation on timeout; add a large-inventory delayed-validation regression proving bounded wall time, durable cursor progress, and no deletion of unvalidated archives. Target files: .agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh. title: Concurrent secret set calls can replace the shared credential inventory
body:
Observed: multiple concurrent aidevops secret set calls targeting the plaintext fallback store caused unrelated pre-existing entries to disappear, leaving only the concurrently rotated pair. Filesystem birth time aligned with the concurrent writers. Root pattern: .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh uses one fixed credentials.sh.tmp path and performs read-filter-move-append updates without inter-process locking. Impact: unrelated API integrations lose access simultaneously; rotating OAuth refresh tokens concurrently can also invalidate the surviving token. Implement: serialize fallback-store mutations with a portable lock, use a unique same-directory mode-0600 temporary file, preserve all unrelated exports, clean up on failure, and keep atomic rename semantics. Also document that token refresh callers must not race the same rotating refresh token. Verification: add a regression that seeds many entries, launches several concurrent set operations, waits for all writers, and proves the full baseline plus every new/updated entry remains exactly once with mode 0600; run ShellCheck and the focused secret-helper test suite.

title: Surface safe session-boundary reminders during sustained interactive loops
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Surface the existing session-lifecycle recommendation at safe pauses so an interactive agent suggests a fresh session after a completed PR lifecycle or 3+ hours, without interrupting active work or ending the session automatically. Preserve a concise continuation checkpoint before recommending `/new`.

## Why

A verified interactive session completed several related PR lifecycles over roughly five hours and accumulated 11 compactions, 4.19M net tokens, 667 introspected calls, and $56.09 reported cost. The detailed policy already says to suggest a new session after PR merge or 3+ hours, but that on-demand reference was not surfaced during the loop. Compaction continuity worked; the missing control was a safe-boundary reminder.

## Evidence and deduplication

- Existing policy: `.agents/reference/session.md` Session Lifecycle.
- Existing compaction continuity: #27498 and its merged implementation; do not duplicate or replace it.
- Searches for PR-merge/three-hour session reminders found no existing issue.
- OpenAI intent tracing is separately addressed by #30941 / PR #30949 and is out of scope.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

Inspect `.agents/reference/session.md`, `.agents/AGENTS.md`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-lifecycle.mjs`, and focused session/compaction tests. Choose the smallest progressive-disclosure or deterministic-advisory surface that reliably exposes the already-decided policy.

### Complete Write Surface

Do not change compaction authority, auto-continue behavior, merge authorization, or session termination. If a runtime advisory is used, keep state session-scoped and emit it at most once per safe boundary.

### Implementation Steps

1. Confirm whether the rule can remain prompt-level while reliably reaching interactive runtimes; otherwise add a bounded advisory hook.
2. Trigger only after a completed PR lifecycle or elapsed-time threshold at a safe pause.
3. Preserve unresolved tasks, IDs, worktree state, and exact next action in a checkpoint or continuation prompt.
4. Add focused positive and negative tests.

### Hazards and Compatibility

Never interrupt an active tool chain, suggest a reset to headless workers, discard unresolved criteria, widen authority, or repeatedly nag after the user chooses to continue. Do not expose session IDs, paths, prompts, or transcript content.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- Focused OpenCode plugin/session tests for the chosen surface
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`
- `git diff --check`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Interactive sessions receive one concise fresh-session suggestion at an eligible safe pause.
- [ ] Active objectives and related implementation phases continue uninterrupted.
- [ ] A continuation checkpoint preserves mutable identifiers and the next action.
- [ ] Headless sessions and short follow-up conversations are unaffected.
- [ ] Existing compaction and auto-continue tests remain green.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — the policy and safety boundary already exist; implementation must select the smallest reliable delivery surface.

title: Add executable managed GitHub comment subcommands
body:
## Problem

The executable managed GitHub helper supports issue/PR create and edit, but not issue/PR comments. Agents operating under OpenCode command policy therefore cannot use the canonical `gh_issue_comment` and `gh_pr_comment` functions without dynamically sourcing shell libraries, which command policy correctly blocks.

During a managed-repository evidence publication, attempts using sourced functions and multiline launcher shapes were blocked. The eventual safe route used the executable gh shim with a pre-signed stdin body, but that bypasses the clearer fixed-action interface established for create/edit.

## Evidence and deduplication

- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh` exposes fixed create/edit actions only.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` already owns `gh_issue_comment` and `gh_pr_comment`, including signatures, public-write guards, timeout handling, instrumentation, and REST fallback.
- Closed #30964 added executable managed create subcommands.
- Closed #28790 / PR #28792 added stdin bodies and executable safe edits.
- Exact open-issue searches found no issue for executable managed comment subcommands.

## Deliverable

Add executable issue and PR comment actions to `gh-write-helper.sh`, delegating to the existing managed comment functions without adding another transport, signature implementation, or policy bypass.

Expected interface:

```text
gh-write-helper.sh issue comment <number-or-url> [managed comment options]
gh-write-helper.sh pr comment <number-or-url> [managed comment options]
```

Both path-backed bodies and `--body-file -` stdin must work through the existing wrappers.

## Implementation guidance

### Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh` — extend usage and the fixed resource/action dispatcher.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh` — add offline executable-comment routing and body cases using existing stubs.
- `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md` — document the executable comment path.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` only if its existing action allowlist requires a narrow update; do not broaden arbitrary shell or raw GitHub writes.

### Required behavior

1. Accept only the fixed `issue|pr` crossed with `create|edit|comment` matrix.
2. Dispatch issue comments directly to `gh_issue_comment` and PR comments directly to `gh_pr_comment`, forwarding argument arrays unchanged.
3. Preserve create/edit behavior and exit codes.
4. Preserve signature-once handling, body validation, public-write guards, instrumentation, cleanup, timeout, and REST fallback in the existing wrapper functions.
5. Support normal body files and `--body-file -` without requiring dynamic `source`, temporary launcher scripts, or raw managed-repository writes.
6. Keep unsupported actions at exit 2 before any GitHub write.

## Hazards

- Do not duplicate comment transport or signature logic in the dispatcher.
- Do not weaken command policy to permit dynamic sourcing.
- Do not log body contents.
- Ensure stdin is consumed exactly once and remains compatible with fallback behavior.
- Do not regress #30964 create actions or #28790 edit/stdin behavior.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-stdin.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

Focused offline tests must prove issue/PR comment routing, path and stdin bodies, signature-once behavior, unsupported-action rejection, and unchanged create/edit behavior. No live GitHub write is required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Executable issue and PR comment actions delegate to the existing managed wrappers.
- [ ] Path-backed and stdin bodies work without dynamic sourcing.
- [ ] Existing signatures, guards, cleanup, timeout, instrumentation, and fallback remain authoritative.
- [ ] Unsupported actions and invalid bodies fail before writes.
- [ ] Create/edit compatibility tests continue to pass.
- [ ] Command policy continues blocking arbitrary source launchers and raw write bypasses.
- [ ] Focused tests, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint pass.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: this adapts the established fixed dispatcher and existing comment wrappers; no trust-boundary redesign is required.
